0. One-Sentence Verdict
The strongest workstation-bounded system would not search possible buildings; it would compile architectural intent, physics, uncertainty, and construction into the coarsest decision-preserving quotient of possible physical worlds, refine only distinctions capable of changing a justified human choice, and materialize complete buildings only as proof witnesses.
I will call the system ANANKE, and its architecture class a Decision-Quotient Engineering Compiler.



1. The Deepest Flaw in Concordia
Concordia’s deepest remaining assumption is that possible buildings are still the primary objects of computation.
Its buildings are sophisticated objects:
partial rather than complete;
behavioral rather than merely geometric;
proof-carrying;
grouped into families;
transformed by lawful rewrites;
analyzed at variable fidelity.
But Concordia still fundamentally asks:
Which building family should be refined, simulated, transformed, optimized, or rejected?
That is already far better than optimizing one BIM model. It is not yet the theoretical upper bound.
ANANKE asks a prior question:
Which distinctions among all possible buildings are capable of changing feasibility, safety, evidence, architectural meaning, or the eventual human decision?
If two billion realizations remain indistinguishable under every currently admissible engineering context, uncertainty model, architectural-intent test, evidence requirement, and stakeholder choice rule, ANANKE does not store a family containing two billion members.
It stores one semantic state.
It does not merely say the members have similar performance. It says:
Until a concrete counterexample demonstrates otherwise, these alternatives are substitutable in every decision-relevant context.
Concordia treats behavioral-equivalence compression as one useful capability among many. ANANKE makes decision-relative contextual equivalence the authoritative meaning of its internal representation.
That changes the governing complexity measure.
For Concordia, complexity is ultimately related to how many unresolved families and analyses remain.
For ANANKE, complexity is governed primarily by:
How many bits of decision-relevant information must cross the boundaries between subsystems?
I will call that quantity decision-separator width.
A hotel can contain hundreds of thousands of components and admit 1050 nominal combinations, yet still be computationally tractable if each local region can be summarized to the rest of the project by a small contract such as:
force-displacement envelope;
heat-flow response;
airflow and pressure response;
route capacity;
fire boundary behavior;
construction-access demand;
maintenance replacement envelope;
cost and lead-time distribution;
architectural equivalence class;
unresolved evidence obligations.
Concordia is a superhuman counterfactual laboratory that asks millions of “what if?” questions.
ANANKE first proves which of those questions are actually different questions.



2. The True Computational Problem
Let:
G be the finite but astronomically large set of realizations generated by an explicitly bounded engineering grammar G;
\(\mathcal I\) be the architect-approved sovereignty theory defining protected, bounded, negotiable, and machine-free intent;
\(\mathcal M\) be the admissible set of physical, economic, regulatory, and empirical models;
 be the admissible future scenarios and uncertainties;
\(\mathcal D\) be the admissible set of human decision functionals, including partial preferences and incomparable values;
E be the current evidence state;
B be the fixed compute budget of the workstation;
AG be the small portfolio eventually shown to humans.
A decision functional \(d\in\mathcal D\) need not be a weighted score. It may be a rule such as:
never violate protected arrival-sequence relationships;
minimize capital cost subject to an outage threshold;
prefer the most adaptable member among designs within 3% of minimum cost;
reject any design dependent on unresolved fire-code interpretation;
preserve several genuinely incomparable choices for owner review.
For a realization x, model m, and evidence state E, let

Jd,m,E(x)
denote the lowest defensible value of x under decision functional d, accounting for uncertainty and evidence limitations.
The regret of returning portfolio A is approximately:
\[ \mathcal R(A,E) = \sup_{d\in\mathcal D,\;m\in\mathcal M} \left[ \sup_{x\in\Omega_G\cap\mathcal I} J_{d,m}(x) - \sup_{a\in A}\underline J_{d,m,E}(a) \right]. \]
ANANKE’s theoretical target is not “find the perfect building.” It is:
\[ \pi_B^\star = \arg\min_{\pi:\operatorname{cost}(\pi)\le B} \left[ \mathbb E\mathcal R(A_\pi,E_\pi) + \lambda_S U_{\mathrm{safety}}(E_\pi) + \lambda_H H_{\mathrm{unresolved}}(E_\pi) \right], \]
where:
 is the policy deciding what the computer should calculate;
A is the final portfolio produced by that policy;
Usafety measures unresolved safety-critical obligations;
Hunresolved measures remaining human-decision burden;
\(\operatorname{cost}(\pi)\) includes time, RAM, VRAM, SSD traffic, energy, and delayed decision cost.
The strongest attainable finite-compute output is therefore an:
-choice-complete evidence portfolio
A portfolio A is -choice-complete when:
For every admitted human decision functional d, at least one member of A has certified regret no greater than d.
Every discarded realization family has an attached certificate showing one of:
infeasibility;
protected-intent violation;
certified dominance;
equivalence to a retained family;
inability to become uniquely preferable by more than d;
unresolved status explicitly preserved rather than falsely eliminated.
Every claim made about a retained design is typed as proof, bound, simulation, empirical evidence, code interpretation, professional judgment, or unresolved uncertainty.
The computer can explain which additional computations could still change the choice.
This reframes whole-building synthesis as:
Compile an enormous realization grammar into a tiny, evidence-bearing decision cover while spending computation only on distinctions that can alter that cover.



3. Theoretical Limits
￼
Several existing theories establish fragments of the proposed direction. Abstract interpretation provides a lattice-based framework for conservatively evaluating sets of program states; CEGAR refines abstractions when counterexamples expose lost distinctions; e-graphs compactly represent many equivalent expressions; variable-elimination complexity is often governed by graph width rather than raw variable count; reduced port spaces can compress component behavior at interfaces; and rational metareasoning formalizes the expected value of additional computation. ACM Digital Library
ANANKE’s claim is not that those established methods already solve building synthesis.
The conjecture is that they point toward a deeper common principle:
The true size of an engineering problem is the size of its smallest decision-sufficient semantics, not the size of its nominal design space.



4. Ten or More Radical Candidate Paradigms
4.1 Generative-program supercompilation
Premise
Represent a building as a typed generative program. Search programs rather than explicit geometry. Use partial evaluation, common-subexpression elimination, recursion, macros, and program transformation to compress repeated floors, rooms, structural bays, and systems.
Source of leverage
A program can describe a trillion geometric instances in a few kilobytes. Repetition becomes a loop rather than duplicated objects. Construction logic, geometry, and physics generation can share parameters.
What kills it
Program-space search is still search over realizations. Two very different programs may have indistinguishable engineering consequences, while two nearly identical programs may cross a critical equipment or code threshold.
Semantic equivalence of arbitrary programs is generally too difficult. A program representation also risks preserving irrelevant implementation distinctions merely because they have different syntax.
Salvage
Use a typed generative language as ANANKE’s source language, but never treat programs themselves as the final semantic identity.



4.2 Constructive proof-first synthesis
Premise
Treat a building as a constructive proof that an artifact satisfying a specification exists. Geometry, products, and details are witnesses extracted from the proof.
Source of leverage
Logical propagation can eliminate impossible families without simulation. Every refinement preserves obligations. Release evidence is native rather than attached later.
What kills it
Buildings are not defined entirely by theorem-like specifications. Uncertain futures, model discrepancy, costs, incomplete code interpretations, and architectural judgment cannot all be reduced honestly to propositions.
Moreover, proof search can simply move the combinatorial explosion into the space of lemmas and witnesses.
Salvage
Make every elimination and transformation evidence-bearing, but allow multiple evidence types rather than pretending everything is mathematically proved.



4.3 Abstract physical interpretation with CEGAR
Premise
Interpret enormous families of buildings through conservative abstract states:
interval geometry;
zonotopic loads;
symbolic routes;
capacity envelopes;
abstract product classes;
uncertain physics ranges.
When an abstraction is too coarse, a counterexample causes refinement.
Source of leverage
One abstract state can conservatively represent millions of realizations. If its optimistic bound is infeasible or dominated, the whole family disappears.
This extends the logic of abstract interpretation and counterexample-guided abstraction refinement into engineering. ACM Digital Library
What kills it
A fixed library of abstract domains becomes the bottleneck. If the abstraction does not match the project’s actual causal structure, intervals become uselessly broad and CEGAR degenerates toward concrete enumeration.
Salvage
Sound set semantics and counterexample-driven splitting are essential, but the machine must also invent project-specific abstractions.



4.4 Equality-saturated engineering
Premise
Place every equivalent formulation of a building subsystem into an engineering e-graph:
algebraically equivalent structural models;
interchangeable network representations;
route rewrites;
equivalent construction decompositions;
geometry transformations;
alternative solver formulations.
Apply rewrites without committing prematurely to one sequence.
Source of leverage
Equality saturation avoids the phase-ordering problem in which one early transformation prevents a better later transformation. E-graphs are designed to represent many equivalent expressions through shared equivalence classes. arXiv
What kills it
Ordinary equality is too strong in some places and too weak in others.
Two systems need not be mathematically identical to be interchangeable for the current decision. Conversely, approximate physical equivalence may fail under an unseen context. Uncontrolled e-graph saturation can also explode in memory.
Salvage
Use bounded, contextual saturation inside small regions of ANANKE’s quotient circuit. Do not make one global e-graph the whole building brain.



4.5 Knowledge-compiled hybrid decision circuits
Premise
Compile logical, discrete, probabilistic, and optimization structure into a circuit supporting rapid repeated queries.
Variables are eliminated. Repeated subproblems are shared. Queries such as feasibility, counting, best completion, and conditional choice become circuit evaluations.
Source of leverage
Knowledge compilation can make repeated inference cheap after an expensive compilation. Variable elimination reveals that raw variable count is often less important than the width of the dependency structure. arXiv
What kills it
Conventional tractable circuits are not designed for geometry-changing PDEs, model discrepancy, continuous high-dimensional fields, or human architectural intent. High dependency width can make compilation explode.
Salvage
Use a hybrid circuit as the backbone, but invent new node semantics for physical operators, evidence, contextual equivalence, and continuous abstract domains.



4.6 The port-operator universe
Premise
Never repeatedly simulate interiors. Represent every subsystem by its boundary behavior:
\[ \text{boundary conditions} \longmapsto \text{boundary responses and internal claims}. \]
A structural bay exposes stiffness and failure envelopes. A room exposes thermal, acoustic, airflow, lighting, occupancy, and service responses. A shaft exposes flow capacity, fire behavior, access, and routing constraints.
Source of leverage
Local systems can be condensed, reduced, and reused. Repeated floors and rooms reuse the same operators. Global analysis becomes interface composition rather than full reconstruction.
Certified port reduction and static condensation already demonstrate that interface spaces can sometimes converge rapidly, while compositional open-system formalisms provide a mathematical language for gluing systems along boundaries. arXiv
What kills it
Not every behavior is local or low-dimensional. Fire, wind, progressive collapse, smoke, turbulent flow, controls, and human movement can produce long-range nonlinear dependencies. An operator library alone also does not solve topology, intent, or decision allocation.
Salvage
Proof-carrying port envelopes become ANANKE’s numerical semantics, with forced escalation when an interface representation loses validity.



4.7 Causal-intervention synthesis
Premise
Search causal mechanisms rather than configurations.
Instead of trying “move wall 73 mm,” discover interventions such as:
align repeating module phases;
break a single-point failure domain;
relocate a high-load subsystem across a structural separator;
create a service-access corridor;
synchronize product thresholds;
decouple construction packages.
Thousands of geometric witnesses may implement one intervention.
Source of leverage
The effective causal dimension can be far lower than the geometric dimension. One intervention can explain large cross-disciplinary effects.
What kills it
The correct causal variables are not given. They are context dependent and may emerge only after detailed analysis. A hand-designed causal ontology would encode current human assumptions and could exclude novel mechanisms.
Salvage
ANANKE must discover and validate causal sufficient statistics automatically.



4.8 Hierarchical renormalization
Premise
Replace microscopic detail with effective theories at progressively larger scales:
fitting and connection;
service rack;
room;
bay;
floor;
vertical stack;
building;
site.
Each scale transmits only effective quantities needed by the next.
Source of leverage
Repeated local detail vanishes into compact large-scale laws. A thousand fixtures may become a small hydraulic response; hundreds of façade panels may become effective thermal, moisture, and structural operators.
What kills it
There is no universal building renormalization operator. Discrete product thresholds, egress rules, access constraints, rare failures, and architectural exceptions can prevent clean scale separation.
Salvage
Use project-specific coarse-graining and retain explicit exception channels. Never assume universal low-rank behavior.



4.9 Tensorized design families
Premise
Represent enormous high-dimensional response functions using tensor trains, hierarchical tensors, or related low-rank factorizations.
Source of leverage
When interactions are structured and ranks remain low, a function defined over billions of combinations can be stored and queried through small tensor cores. Tensor-network methods can avoid dense storage of high-dimensional arrays in favorable cases. arXiv
What kills it
Catalog discontinuities, rare failure states, topology changes, contact, and highly coupled constraints can cause rank explosion. Approximation error may also be concentrated exactly in safety-critical corners.
Salvage
Use tensor compression for local response tables, uncertainty maps, and repeated operators—never as the sole authoritative representation.



4.10 Adversarial theorem game
Premise
Alternate between:
a synthesizer proposing the least complicated realization family satisfying current obligations;
an adversary finding the smallest plausible counterexample that invalidates a claim.
The design acquires complexity only when failure search proves that complexity necessary.
Source of leverage
It avoids adding redundancy, detail, and conservative complexity without evidence. Minimal counterexamples expose deep weaknesses more efficiently than random simulation.
What kills it
The game may converge to a merely feasible artifact rather than an excellent one. It can cycle, overfit to known adversaries, and struggle with incomparable human values.
Salvage
Use adversarial counterexamples as the principal refinement mechanism, but retain decision coverage and tradeoff reasoning.



4.11 Rational computation market
Premise
Treat every possible analysis, proof, split, simulation, or human query as an action with an expected value of computation.
Source of leverage
The system stops spending hours on analyses that cannot change the decision and prioritizes cheap calculations capable of killing huge branches. Rational metareasoning formalizes this general idea. ar5iv
What kills it
Metareasoning does not change the underlying representation. An exquisitely scheduled brute-force optimizer is still brute force. Estimating the value of every computation can itself consume the budget.
Salvage
Make metareasoning subordinate to a much stronger quotient representation and cap its overhead.



4.12 Universal differentiable engineering IR
Premise
Compile continuous, discrete, symbolic, and topological decisions into relaxed differentiable forms. Use gradients throughout.
Source of leverage
Gradients can move thousands of continuous variables using relatively few physics solves.
What kills it
Discrete thresholds, topology, remeshing, code logic, product availability, contact, and human sovereignty do not become trustworthy merely because they have smooth relaxations. A relaxed optimum may have no valid physical witness.
Salvage
Use gradients inside topology-stable quotient cells and reduced operators, never as the global semantics.



4.13 Decision-quotient compilation — the winner
Premise
Compile the entire realization grammar into a circuit whose states are equivalence classes under all decision-relevant contexts.
A distinction is retained only when it can change:
hard feasibility;
safety;
evidence status;
architectural sovereignty;
robust preference;
inclusion in the final decision cover.
Source of leverage
It attacks the source of combinatorial cost before search begins.
It uses:
program grammars for generation;
abstract interpretation for set semantics;
e-graph-like congruence for shared rewrites;
knowledge compilation for variable elimination;
port operators for physics;
CEGAR for splitting;
adversaries for failure discovery;
metareasoning for compute allocation.
But these are not equal ingredients in a Frankenstein architecture.
They are subordinate implementations of one principle:
Preserve only decision-relevant distinguishability.
What could kill it
If realistic buildings have intrinsically large decision-separator width—meaning that almost every local distinction can affect the global decision—then the quotient remains enormous and ANANKE collapses toward Concordia.
That is the architecture’s central falsifiable conjecture.



5. The Winning Paradigm
ANANKE: the Decision-Quotient Engineering Compiler
ANANKE consists of eleven interacting systems.
5.1 Typed source theory
The source is not BIM. It is an executable theory containing:
the site and environmental conditions;
a finite generative grammar of realizations;
physical laws and engineering models;
product and assembly catalogs;
codes and interpretations;
construction and maintenance processes;
uncertainty models;
architectural sovereignty;
decision rules;
evidence requirements.
The grammar can generate geometry, but geometry is not generated by default.



5.2 Sovereignty type checker
Before engineering compilation, architectural transformations are classified as:
definitionally equivalent;
architecturally equivalent;
bounded;
approval-requiring;
forbidden;
machine-free.
Illegal transformations are removed from the source language before optimization.



5.3 Decision-Quotient Argument Circuit
The source theory compiles into ANANKE’s authoritative internal object:
The Decision-Quotient Argument Circuit, or DQAC.
It is a persistent hybrid circuit containing:
choice nodes;
parameter-domain nodes;
subsystem-composition nodes;
logical constraints;
physical response relations;
universal uncertainty nodes;
adversarial failure nodes;
architectural-intent predicates;
evidence nodes;
proof certificates;
equivalence classes;
refinement boundaries;
witness-generation recipes.
A DQAC node does not mean “this wall exists.”
It means something closer to:
There exists a family of realizations with this boundary behavior, consequence envelope, sovereignty status, and evidence state.



5.4 Contextual quotient engine
The quotient engine continually asks whether two circuit regions can be merged.
It looks for equivalence under:
all presently relevant neighboring systems;
all protected intent tests;
all live uncertainty scenarios;
all decision functionals capable of affecting the output portfolio;
all active evidence obligations.
Classes split only when a counterexample establishes a meaningful distinction.



5.5 Proof-carrying physical operator compiler
Local physics is compiled into reusable interface objects:
stiffness and compliance operators;
thermal transfer operators;
pressure-flow relations;
electrical impedance and protection envelopes;
acoustic transfer matrices;
moisture and leakage envelopes;
construction precedence automata;
maintenance-access contracts;
cost, lead-time, and carbon distributions.
The compiler can generate ordinary FEM, CFD, energy, or network models when needed, but it tries to retain only the resulting decision-sufficient boundary semantics.



5.6 Abstract consequence engine
This engine evaluates entire realization classes using:
exact logic;
symbolic algebra;
intervals;
affine arithmetic;
convex relaxations;
reduced bases;
low-rank tensors;
conservative neural residuals;
partial-order bounds.
It tracks what is:
certainly true;
certainly false;
possible;
unresolved;
irrelevant to the current decision.



5.7 Decision-boundary manager
ANANKE does not maintain a conventional Pareto archive unless the decision theory explicitly requires one.
It maintains a choice boundary:
classes that might still be selected under some admissible stakeholder preference;
classes whose uncertainty could move them onto or off that boundary;
classes excluded with certificates;
classes equivalent for every admitted choice.
This can be much smaller than a dense Pareto frontier.



5.8 Regret-closure metareasoner
Every possible computation is evaluated by its expected ability to:
close decision regret;
eliminate a large quotient region;
resolve safety-critical uncertainty;
distinguish apparently equivalent classes;
discharge an evidence obligation;
create a reusable abstraction;
reduce future computation.



5.9 Witness synthesizer
Only near the end does the machine extract complete buildings.
A witness is generated by solving the residual existential constraints inside a surviving quotient class:

x(Q)s.t.xrealizesthecertifiedboundaryandintentcontracts.
Several geometrically different witnesses may come from the same semantic class.



5.10 Adversarial claim breaker
The adversary does not merely attack a geometric candidate.
It attacks individual claims:
“single equipment failure affects fewer than 20 rooms”;
“this route remains maintainable under allowed substitutions”;
“construction sequencing never blocks fire access”;
“the envelope remains within moisture limits”;
“this class is behaviorally equivalent to that class.”
A successful counterexample refines the DQAC.



5.11 Evidence ledger
Every conclusion is linked to:
assumptions;
model versions;
numerical tolerances;
approximation bounds;
empirical calibration;
code interpretation;
professional approval;
dependencies;
invalidation conditions.
The ledger covers the entire search, not merely the final release.



6. The One Big Idea
A normal optimizer evaluates buildings.
Concordia evaluates partially resolved building families.
ANANKE compiles away the need for most buildings to be represented at all.
Suppose there are ten million possible internal arrangements for a guestroom service zone. To the rest of the hotel, those arrangements may expose only:
12 possible shaft-demand envelopes;
8 structural-penetration patterns;
5 acoustic classes;
7 maintenance-access classes;
4 cost bands;
3 architectural equivalence classes.
The global system does not need ten million arrangements.
It may need only a few hundred valid combinations of those interface signatures.
It eliminates the internal variables and stores the resulting boundary relation.
If later analysis shows that two arrangements previously grouped together behave differently under an unusual supplier substitution, fire condition, or maintenance operation, the class splits.
Until then, their difference does not exist computationally.
The equivalent of the breakthrough is:
Dynamic programming over physical meaning, where the state variable is the smallest information needed to preserve every possible downstream engineering decision.
The machine appears to search an astronomical space.
In reality, it recursively asks:
What is the minimum sufficient message this region must send to the rest of the building?
Everything else is compiled away.



7. Fundamental Mathematical Representation
7.1 Realization grammar
Let G be a finite typed grammar whose programs generate physically interpretable realizations:
\[ \Omega_G=\{x\mid x\text{ is generated by }G\}. \]
A realization contains geometry only when its grammar is expanded sufficiently.
Early terms may represent:
an unresolved service region;
a family of structural systems;
a vertical-distribution mechanism;
a construction-access strategy;
a class of façades;
an unresolved room-stack program.



7.2 Contexts
A context C[-] is any admissible surrounding system into which a partial realization can be inserted.
For a shaft subsystem, contexts may vary:
floor count;
room arrangement;
fire zones;
structural system;
pressure conditions;
maintenance requirements;
product substitutions;
stakeholder decisions.



7.3 Observations
For partial realization p, define its observation under context C, model m, and scenario  as:
\[ \mathsf{Obs}(C[p],m,\xi) = (Y,\;H,\;A,\;E), \]
where:
Y is a consequence envelope;
H is hard-feasibility status;
A is architectural-sovereignty status;
E is evidence status.
The consequence envelope may include cost, energy, carbon, reliability, usable area, schedule, maintainability, and other quantities, but it is not reduced to one scalar.



7.4 Decision-relative contextual congruence
Two partial realizations p and q are exactly contextually equivalent when:
\[ p\equiv_{\mathcal T}q \iff \forall C\in\mathcal C_{\mathcal T}, \forall m\in\mathcal M, \forall \xi\in\Xi, \forall d\in\mathcal D: \]\[ \mathsf{Choice}_d \left( \mathsf{Obs}(C[p],m,\xi) \right) = \mathsf{Choice}_d \left( \mathsf{Obs}(C[q],m,\xi) \right), \]
and their hard, sovereignty, and evidence classifications agree.
An approximate form permits bounded differences only when those differences provably cannot alter any active decision:
\[ p\equiv_{\mathcal T}^{\varepsilon}q \iff \Delta_d(p,q)\le\varepsilon_d \quad \text{and no hard/evidence boundary can be crossed.} \]
The quotient is:
\[ \mathcal Q_{\mathcal T} = \Omega_G/\equiv_{\mathcal T}. \]
ANANKE’s authoritative state is a compressed representation of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathcal T}\), not of G.



7.5 The Decision-Quotient Argument Circuit
Each DQAC node denotes a relation:

RnBninBnoutYnEn,
where:
Bnin and Bnout are boundary states;
Yn is the consequence envelope;
En is the evidence object.
Node types include:
￼
The circuit shares repeated subexpressions aggressively. Eight identical guestroom floors do not produce eight independent semantic graphs.



7.6 Decision-separator width
Consider partitioning the building problem into regions L and R, separated by interface S.
Let \(\Sigma_S^\mathcal T\) be the smallest set of messages that preserves every decision-relevant consequence transmitted between L and R.
For discrete messages, define:
\[ w_D(S)=\log_2|\Sigma_S^\mathcal T|. \]
For continuous messages, use the logarithm of the minimum covering number required at decision tolerance :
\[ w_D^\varepsilon(S) = \log_2 \mathcal N_\varepsilon \left( \Sigma_S^\mathcal T \right). \]
The project’s decision-separator width is:

WD=validdecompositionsSwD(S).
The central conjecture is:
\[ \text{Practical synthesis cost} \approx \operatorname{poly}(N) \cdot 2^{W_D^\varepsilon}, \]
rather than:
\[ \operatorname{cost} \propto |\Omega_G|. \]
This does not make every problem easy. It identifies the real enemy.
The enemy is not “billions of variables.”
The enemy is a boundary requiring too much decision-relevant information.



7.7 What actually exists in memory
ANANKE stores:
interned generative terms;
canonical topology fragments;
quotient-class identifiers;
factor scopes and separator maps;
discrete decision-diagram nodes;
intervals, polytopes, zonotopes, and symbolic domains;
low-rank operator coefficients;
reduced bases;
lower and upper consequence envelopes;
proof and evidence pointers;
invalidation dependencies;
cold-object content hashes;
witness recipes.
It generally does not store:
one mesh per building;
one BIM model per candidate;
complete geometry for every floor;
one simulation state per product combination;
one copy of every repeated room;
a dense table over all uncertainties;
a full Pareto point for every realization.



8. Newly Invented Mathematics
8.1 Decision-Relative Contextual Congruence
Status: Extrapolated foundation; strongest compactness properties are conjectural.
Purpose: Eliminate distinctions among realizations that cannot alter an admissible decision.
Mathematical object: An equivalence or bounded pseudometric relation over partial realization programs, parameterized by a set of contexts, models, scenarios, evidence obligations, and decision functionals.
Operation: Compare two partial systems through:
canonical symbolic tests;
boundary-operator equivalence;
hard-constraint equivalence;
architectural-intent equivalence;
adversarial distinguishing searches.
Composition rule: The relation must be a congruence:
\[ p\equiv q \Longrightarrow C[p]\equiv C[q] \]
for all admitted contexts C.
Refinement rule: A counterexample C showing different decision consequences splits the class:
\[ [p] \longrightarrow [p]_{C^\star} \cup [q]_{C^\star}. \]
Error semantics: Approximate merging is permitted only when the maximum possible difference cannot cross any feasibility, evidence, or choice boundary.
Complexity conjecture: Real building systems contain enormous syntactic diversity but relatively few decision-distinguishable interface behaviors.
Implementation: Union-find structures for exact equivalence; hashed canonical signatures; SMT certificates; interval operator comparisons; adversarial distinguishing queries.
Failure mode: Hidden contexts may distinguish merged systems.
Fallback: Certified merges require proof or conservative bounds. Unproven merges remain heuristic proposal clusters and may not justify pruning.



8.2 Decision-Separator Width
Status: Extrapolated from treewidth, sufficient statistics, information bottlenecks, and interface reduction; building-specific theory is conjectural.
Purpose: Replace raw design-space size with a meaningful complexity parameter.
Mathematical object: The minimum information capacity of separator variables needed to preserve all admitted downstream decisions.
Operation: Search for a separator statistic:

z=(xS)
such that internal variables on one side of the separator become decision-irrelevant given z.
Operationally:
\[ Y_L \perp X_R \mid z \]
need not hold probabilistically in the ordinary sense. What must hold is that all admissible consequences of L on Rfactor through z.
Composition rule: Adjacent regions exchange only separator statistics.
Refinement rule: If a counterexample shows that z omitted relevant information, expand or split z.
Error semantics: A residual dependence envelope records what was not captured.
Complexity conjecture: Whole-building synthesis is tractable on a workstation when project-specific abstractions can keep WD moderate.
Implementation: Graph separators, variable elimination, symbolic regression, operator rank tests, proof-trace mining, and active counterexample search.
Failure mode: Global effects cause the separator statistic to become enormous.
Fallback: Widen the separator, merge fewer regions, and escalate to conventional coupled analysis.



8.3 Decision-Quotient Argument Circuits
Status: Extrapolated from knowledge compilation, factor graphs, decision diagrams, e-graphs, and proof DAGs.
Purpose: Give continuous, discrete, symbolic, topological, physical, uncertain, and evidentiary reasoning one shared intermediate representation.
Mathematical object: A typed directed acyclic hypergraph whose nodes denote relations over boundary states, consequence envelopes, and evidence.
Operations:
conjunction and relational join;
existential elimination;
universal scenario quantification;
min/max or partial-order aggregation;
contextual quotienting;
operator composition;
proof attachment;
witness extraction.
Composition rule: Shared boundary variables are joined and then eliminated:
\[ R_{A\circ B} = \exists z\; R_A(x,z) \land R_B(z,y). \]
For numerical operators, the corresponding operation may be a Schur complement, transfer composition, convolution, or reduced nonlinear solve.
Refinement rule: Replace one abstract node with a subcircuit whose union conservatively equals the original concretization.
Error semantics: Every approximate node carries a consequence envelope and an influence certificate.
Complexity conjecture: The circuit remains compact when repeated motifs, low-width separators, and contextual equivalences dominate.
Implementation: A heterogeneous store combining:
BDD/SDD-like nodes;
interval and affine domains;
sparse factor tables;
low-rank tensors;
symbolic expressions;
reduced numerical operators;
proof pointers.
Failure mode: Circuit width or node count explodes.
Fallback: Evict cold branches, use bounded-width approximate elimination, or revert to branch-and-bound for the affected region.



8.4 Proof-Carrying Port Envelopes
Status: Known foundations plus extrapolated multiphysics composition; universal compactness is conjectural.
Purpose: Eliminate repeated full simulation of nearly identical subsystem interiors.
Mathematical object: For subsystem family S,
\[ \mathcal P_S: (b,\theta,\xi) \longmapsto \left\{ r,\;y,\;e \right\}, \]
where:
b is the boundary condition;
 is an unresolved design parameter;
 is uncertainty;
r is boundary response;
y is internal consequence;
e is evidence and error status.
The stored object may be:
an exact matrix;
a symbolic transfer function;
a reduced basis;
an interval relation;
a monotone graph;
a polynomial/rational approximation;
a tensor train;
a neural residual with certified outer bounds.
Composition rule: Glue ports, enforce compatibility and conservation, then eliminate the shared state.
For linear structure:

Keff=Kbb-KbiKii-1Kib.
For network systems, compose flow-pressure relations and eliminate internal nodes.
Refinement rule: Split parameter domains, add basis vectors, increase precision, or run a local full-order solve.
Error semantics: Residual estimators and validity domains travel with the operator.
Complexity conjecture: Many repeated building subsystems have low-dimensional boundary behavior even when their interiors are detailed.
Implementation: Dense or sparse reduced matrices, basis vectors, interpolation coefficients, interval residuals, and content-addressed provenance.
Failure mode: Strong nonlinearities, rare events, or global modes make the envelope broad or high rank.
Fallback: Full local or global simulation; the resulting solve enriches the operator instead of being discarded.



8.5 Rewrite-Functor Jets
Status: Conjectural synthesis of incremental computation, shape derivatives, topological derivatives, cospan-like rewrites, and solution transport.
Purpose: Preserve knowledge across topology changes.
Mathematical object: A topology rewrite is represented as a span:

AKB,
where K is the common semantic interface preserved by both topologies.
Attached to the rewrite is a jet:

Jr=(Tx,T,TV,TP,TE,r),
containing transport maps for:
primal states x;
dual variables ;
reduced bases V;
preconditioners P;
evidence dependencies E;
residual change r.
Operation: Reuse unchanged factors exactly, transport compatible boundary state, and recompute only the rewrite’s affected separator closure.
Composition rule:

Jr2r1Jr2Jr1,
with residual bounds accumulated explicitly.
Refinement rule: If transported states produce excessive residual, expand the affected region or cold-start that region.
Error semantics: The jet provides a residual certificate showing how far the transported state lies from a valid new solution.
Complexity conjecture: For local rewrites, update cost scales with affected separator size rather than total building size.
Implementation: Persistent factor graphs, structural hashes, sparse projection/prolongation maps, low-rank updates, and dependency-indexed cache invalidation.
Failure mode: A local topology change triggers a global mode change.
Fallback: The dependency closure expands to the full model. Nothing is silently reused beyond its validity.



8.6 Decision-Influence Error Calculus
Status: Extrapolated from interval analysis, sensitivity analysis, abstract interpretation, and goal-oriented error estimation.
Purpose: Stop refining numerical values whose remaining error cannot affect the decision.
Mathematical object: Each approximation carries not only a norm error
\[ \|y-\hat y\|\le\delta, \]
but a decision-influence set:
\[ \mathcal I_E = \left\{ d\in\mathcal D: \delta\text{ could alter }d \right\}. \]
Operation: Push errors through the DQAC using:
local Lipschitz bounds;
adjoint sensitivities;
interval propagation;
monotonicity;
correlation-aware affine forms;
threshold-distance calculations.
Composition rule: Errors compose according to dependency structure rather than being naïvely added as independent or worst-case quantities.
Refinement rule: Increase fidelity only where the error cone intersects a live feasibility, evidence, or choice boundary.
Error semantics: Native by definition.
Complexity conjecture: Most numerical precision sought in engineering optimization is decision-irrelevant.
Implementation: Compact interval vectors, sparse influence bitsets, threshold-distance caches, and adjoint projections.
Failure mode: Error correlations or nonlinear amplification are underestimated.
Fallback: Conservative outer bounds; if uncertain, mark the computation as decision-relevant and refine.



8.7 Causal Sufficient-Separator Synthesis
Status: Conjectural.
Purpose: Allow the system to invent operational abstractions such as “wet-service spine” or “replacement-access bottleneck.”
Mathematical object: A proposed macro variable

z=(XS)
that compresses a group of detailed variables XS while preserving downstream consequences.
Operation: Search for  by combining:
repeated proof patterns;
common sensitivity directions;
low-rank operator structure;
symbolic expressions;
graph cuts;
intervention tests;
minimum-description-length criteria.
Composition rule: Replace the original factor cluster with a typed macro factor exposing z.
Refinement rule: Counterexamples split the macro or add state dimensions.
Error semantics: A residual relation states what consequences are not fully mediated by z.
Complexity conjecture: Mature engineering domains contain many unnamed low-dimensional sufficient mechanisms.
Implementation: Symbolic regression, sparse basis discovery, partition refinement, small graph neural proposal models, and deterministic verification.
Failure mode: The discovered abstraction fits sampled cases but fails under rare conditions.
Fallback: It remains a heuristic proposal until adversarially validated. Unvalidated abstractions may guide search but cannot justify elimination.



8.8 Regret-Closure Value of Computation
Status: Extrapolated from rational metareasoning; the building-specific formulation is new.
Purpose: Select the next computation by its expected effect on the final decision, not by generic uncertainty or model error.
Let current state be Q, with certified decision regret \(\mathcal R(Q)\).
For computation c with possible results o, define:
\[ \operatorname{RCVOC}(c\mid Q) = \frac{ \mathcal R(Q) - \mathbb E_o[ \mathcal R(\operatorname{Update}(Q,c,o)) ] + \alpha\,\mathbb E[\Delta S_c] + \beta\,\mathbb E[\Delta R_c] }{ t_c + \lambda_M m_c + \lambda_V v_c + \lambda_I i_c + \lambda_E e_c }, \]
where:
Sc is safety-obligation closure;
Rc is expected future reuse;
tc is time;
mc is RAM pressure;
vc is VRAM pressure;
ic is SSD traffic;
ec is energy or delayed-decision cost.
Operation: Rank candidate computations using optimistic and pessimistic RCVOC bounds.
Composition rule: Computations with shared setup or reusable results may be bundled.
Refinement rule: Update the RCVOC predictor from observed pruning, regret closure, and runtime.
Complexity conjecture: A low-cost approximate scheduler can capture most of the gains of an intractable exact metareasoner.
Implementation: Deterministic features plus a small learned ranking model.
Failure mode: The scheduler mispredicts and starves important analyses.
Fallback: Mandatory safety queues, fairness budgets, and conservative deterministic escalation policies.



8.9 Sovereignty-Preserving Transformation Logic
Status: Extrapolated from refinement types, formal contracts, partial orders, and user-approved equivalence relations.
Purpose: Preserve architectural authorship without turning beauty into a scalar objective.
Mathematical object: An intent theory
\[ \mathcal I = (P,\;B,\;N,\;F,\;\sim_A), \]
where:
P is protected invariants;
B is bounded variation;
N is negotiable territory;
F is machine-free authorship;
A is the architect-approved equivalence relation.
Operation: Every transformation receives a type judgment:
\[ \Gamma_{\mathcal I}\vdash r:A\to B \;:\; \text{preserving}, \text{bounded}, \text{approval-required}, \text{forbidden}. \]
Composition rule: A sequence remains intent-preserving only if every transformation and emergent composition type-checks.
Refinement rule: Humans may expand or narrow approved equivalence classes.
Error semantics: Perceptual or learned assessments are proposals with uncertainty, never final architectural truth.
Failure mode: Intent is incompletely formalized.
Fallback: Unformalized visible changes require human approval rather than being optimized silently.



9. Search Without Candidate Enumeration
ANANKE’s main loop is not:

generatesimulatescorerepeat.
It is:

compileeliminatedistinctionsboundrefineonlyatdecisionboundaries.
A simplified algorithm is:
Q = compile_source_to_DQAC(grammar, physics, intent, uncertainty, evidence)

while compute_budget_remains:

    propagate_hard_constraints(Q)
    canonicalize_symmetries_and_rewrites(Q)
    eliminate_internal_variables_at_small_separators(Q)
    compose_reusable_port_envelopes(Q)

    merge_classes_with_certified_contextual_equivalence(Q)
    prune_infeasible_or_decision-irrelevant_classes(Q)
    update_decision_regret_and_evidence_frontier(Q)

    if requested stopping condition is satisfied:
        break

    candidate_computations = enumerate_refinements_that_could_change_choice(Q)
    c = select_by_bounded_regret_closure_value(candidate_computations)

    result = execute(c)

    if result is a counterexample:
        split_quotient_class_or_expand_context(Q, result)
    else:
        tighten_bound_or_enrich_operator(Q, result)

return extract_small_epsilon_choice_complete_witness_portfolio(Q)
What gets eliminated without candidates
Exact symmetries
Permutations of identical guestrooms, equivalent floor labels, symmetric shaft assignments, and structurally isomorphic networks are canonicalized.
Internal variables
If a subsystem interacts with the rest of the building only through a small boundary relation, all internal choices are existentially eliminated.
Decision-equivalent realizations
Different systems producing the same admitted boundary consequences and evidence are merged.
Dominated abstract classes
If the optimistic envelope of a class is worse than the certified pessimistic envelope of another class for every admitted decision rule, the class is removed.
Infeasible classes
A conservative proof of infeasibility eliminates every realization in that class.
Numerically irrelevant distinctions
If two response intervals lie safely on the same side of every active threshold, refinement stops.
Does a complete building exist during search?
For most of the computation, no.
ANANKE may temporarily materialize:
a local room geometry;
a representative structural bay;
a route witness;
a reduced simulation mesh;
a partial floor plan;
a candidate separator configuration.
But it does not maintain a complete building for every live state.
Complete buildings appear only when:
a quotient class is competitive;
its internal existential constraints appear satisfiable;
an actual witness is needed for detailed analysis, review, or release.
The witness is not the search state.
It is a compiled output of the search state.



10. Physics Without Repeated Full Simulation
10.1 General principle
For subsystem S, instead of repeatedly solving:

FS(u,,)=0
for every candidate, compile a reusable relation:
\[ \mathcal P_S: (u_{\partial S},\theta,\xi) \mapsto (y_{\partial S},z_S,E_S). \]
The interior variables are condensed away unless they become decision-relevant.



10.2 Structural systems
Early and intermediate stages use:
analytical bounds;
condensed stiffness matrices;
component mode synthesis;
reduced buckling spaces;
interval strength envelopes;
cached nonlinear tangent operators.
Repeated bays reuse the same local operators.
A topology or connection detail requiring nonlinear contact receives a specialized operator or full solve only when it matters.
Global nonlinear collapse, progressive failure, and detailed connection verification remain finalist analyses.



10.3 Thermal and energy systems
Rooms, façade regions, and zones expose:
thermal admittance;
solar-gain transfer;
moisture response;
internal-load envelopes;
state-space dynamics;
control-relevant reduced states.
Repeated floors can be composed through shared transfer operators with low-rank corrections for orientation, corner rooms, occupancy, and exceptions.
Full annual simulations become cross-checks and calibration sources rather than the only way to evaluate every alternative.



10.4 HVAC, plumbing, drainage, and fire protection
Segments expose relations such as:
\[ (\Delta p,\;T_{\mathrm{in}},\;q_{\mathrm{in}}) \mapsto (q_{\mathrm{out}},\;T_{\mathrm{out}},\;\text{noise},\;\text{risk},\;\text{cost}). \]
Networks are assembled by:
conservation;
compatibility;
capacity constraints;
monotone relation composition;
internal-node elimination.
Catalog thresholds remain exact predicates rather than being smoothed away.
Drainage slope, cleanout access, fire separation, and replacement space are carried as logical-geometric port obligations.



10.5 Electrical systems
Equipment and distribution regions expose:
load envelopes;
voltage-drop response;
fault-current ranges;
protective-device compatibility;
redundancy state;
thermal limits;
feeder and pathway demands;
catalog thresholds.
Internal circuit assignments can be eliminated when only aggregate behavior matters. They are expanded when coordination, routing, or failure isolation distinguishes them.



10.6 Façade and envelope
Assembly families expose:
thermal transfer;
solar response;
air leakage;
moisture migration;
structural support demands;
wind-pressure validity domains;
maintenance and replacement access;
embodied carbon and lead time.
Rare details such as corners, parapets, transitions, and penetrations remain explicit exception operators rather than contaminating the entire repeated façade representation.



10.7 Acoustics, lighting, and daylight
Early models use:
transfer matrices;
path-loss bounds;
radiosity or visibility summaries;
spectral response bases;
perceptual threshold envelopes.
High-resolution ray tracing or wave models are used only where uncertainty could alter room classification, architectural intent, or a final claim.



10.8 Construction, maintenance, and lifecycle
These are not PDEs, but they still compile into interface behavior.
A construction package exposes:
prerequisites;
crew and crane demand;
workspace;
temporary stability;
completion state;
inspection obligations;
tolerance propagation;
downstream access.
A maintenance region exposes:
reachability;
clearance;
shutdown domain;
replacement path;
temporary support;

10.9 Where full simulation remains unavoidable
Full or high-fidelity analysis is still needed for selected cases involving:
nonlinear structure;
complex wind;
fire and smoke;
turbulent airflow;
soil-structure interaction;
unusual moisture behavior;
emergent controls;
complex acoustic fields;
coupled transient hazards.
ANANKE’s breakthrough is not abolishing high-fidelity physics.
It is ensuring that high-fidelity physics is invoked for dozens of decision-critical questions rather than millions of barely distinct realizations.



11. Topology Change Without Forgetting Everything
Conventional topology change often destroys:
meshes;
variable numbering;
solver factorizations;
reduced bases;
derivatives;
routes;
references;
proof state.
ANANKE avoids tying knowledge to one monolithic topology.
11.1 Persistent factorized semantics
Every local subsystem has:
a structural hash;
an interface signature;
an operator;
evidence dependencies;
a place in an elimination tree.
A topology rewrite changes a bounded subgraph whenever possible.
Unchanged factors remain bit-for-bit reusable.



11.2 Common-interface rewriting
A rewrite is expressed as:

AKB.
Examples:
one shaft becomes two while floor interfaces remain the same;
a central plant becomes two distributed plants while zone demand ports persist;
one structural bay is split while neighboring supports remain;
a corridor rack moves to the opposite side while room service ports remain.
The common interface K identifies what semantic information survives.



11.3 Persistent elimination tree
Suppose a network’s internal variables have been eliminated through a tree of separator computations.
After a local rewrite:
untouched leaves are retained;
only affected ancestors are invalidated;
the smallest valid separator closure is recomputed;
cached operators outside that closure remain valid.
This is analogous to an incremental compiler or persistent data structure, not a full-model rebuild.



11.4 Transported numerical knowledge
The Rewrite-Functor Jet transports:
compatible primal fields;
dual sensitivities;
local reduced bases;
preconditioner blocks;
uncertainty samples;
proof obligations;
solver trust regions.
A transported result is never accepted merely because it exists. Its residual is measured.
If:
\[ \|F_B(T_x x_A)\|\le\tau, \]
the state may be used as a warm start or certified approximation.
If not, the affected region expands.



11.5 Generalized rewrite differential
For outcome functional J, define a rewrite differential approximately as:
\[ \mathfrak D_r J = J(B) - J(A) - \langle \lambda_A,\Delta_r F\rangle, \]
where rF is the residual introduced by the rewrite after transporting the previous solution.
Unlike an ordinary derivative, \(\mathfrak D_r J\) compares spaces of different topology and dimension through their common semantic interface.
It does not promise exact gradients over arbitrary topology.
Its role is to estimate:
whether a rewrite is likely valuable;
which analyses become invalid;
which solution information survives;
how large the affected computational region may be.



11.6 Worst case
Some changes are genuinely global:
changing structural system;
reversing the building orientation;
replacing all-air HVAC with hydronic terminals;
introducing a new atrium;
changing floor count;
changing the fire strategy.
ANANKE does not claim those are local.
Its guarantee is:
It forgets only what the dependency and residual analysis proves must be forgotten.



12. Automatic Abstraction Discovery
A fixed building ontology cannot be the theoretical endpoint.
ANANKE mines abstractions from its own computation.
12.1 Sources of abstraction evidence
It examines:
variables repeatedly appearing together in proofs;
variables sharing sensitivity directions;
repeated separator messages;
common causes of threshold crossings;
repeated counterexamples;
recurring operator subspaces;
stable low-rank response coordinates;
patterns in successful topology rewrites;
recurring unsatisfiable cores.



12.2 Proposed macro variable
Suppose 80 detailed variables involving:
room widths;
façade joints;
column locations;
bathroom-pod edges;
drainage branches;
rack splice points
repeatedly affect outcomes through a small phase relationship.
ANANKE may propose:
\[ z_{\mathrm{module}} = \left( w_{\mathrm{room}} \bmod p_{\mathrm{façade}}, \; 2w_{\mathrm{room}} \bmod p_{\mathrm{structure}}, \; w_{\mathrm{wetwall}} \bmod p_{\mathrm{rack}} \right). \]
This becomes an operational abstraction such as:
cross-system modular phase lock.
It is not merely a label or embedding.
The new variable can:
drive branching;
derive bounds;
define quotient classes;
formulate rewrites;
explain causal effects;
reduce separator width.



12.3 Validation
A macro is promoted only if ANANKE can show that:
replacing detailed variables by the macro preserves relevant consequences within a bound;
adversarial interventions fail to find a distinguishing case;
the macro improves compression or computation;
the macro has an explicit concretization map back to realizations.
A failed macro is discarded or split.



12.4 Self-improvement without giant training
ANANKE improves primarily by accumulating:
reusable operator bases;
successful separator statistics;
proof macros;
canonical rewrites;
unsatisfiable cores;
discrepancy models;
branching and refinement statistics;
validated motif libraries.
This is closer to a compiler learning optimization passes than a giant model memorizing buildings.
Optional AI components
￼
The language model is loaded on demand and unloaded before VRAM-intensive numerical work.
Hallucinated facts cannot enter the authoritative state without:
provenance;
deterministic parsing;
units;
validation;
or explicit human acceptance.



13. Self-Optimizing Computation
At any point, ANANKE may choose among thousands of actions.
It does not rank them by “uncertainty” alone.
Uncertainty can be irrelevant.
13.1 Decision gaps
Suppose class A has certified cost:
\[ \$81\text{M}\le C_A\le \$82\text{M}, \]
and class B has:
\[ \$93\text{M}\le C_B\le \$101\text{M}, \]
while B is no better on any protected or admitted criterion.
Refining B’s estimate from $96.318 million to $96.302 million has no decision value.
Conversely, a 20-millisecond clearance bound that proves every member of a huge shaft family infeasible may have enormous value.



13.2 Computation actions
Each action advertises:
likely outcomes;
runtime distribution;
RAM and VRAM requirements;
expected circuit region affected;
possible proof obligations closed;
likely classes eliminated;
expected reuse;
risk of discovering model invalidity.
Examples:
tighten a shaft-area lower bound;
split a façade operator domain;
run a structural bay solve;
inspect a code interpretation;
refine a construction-access abstraction;
execute a fire scenario;
ask an architect whether two transformations are equivalent;
build a new reduced basis;
attempt a topology rewrite;
search for a counterexample to a merge.



13.3 RCVOC scheduling
ANANKE estimates:
\[ \operatorname{RCVOC}(c) = \frac{ \text{expected regret reduction} + \text{safety closure} + \text{future reuse} }{ \text{time} + \text{memory pressure} + \text{VRAM pressure} + \text{I/O} + \text{energy} }. \]
It also keeps upper bounds on actions it has not tried recently, preventing premature starvation.



13.4 Mandatory overrides
The scheduler may not indefinitely postpone:
safety-critical unresolved obligations;
validity-domain violations;
evidence expiration;
counterexamples to certified merges;
human decisions blocking major branches.
Metareasoning is a servant, not an excuse to ignore assurance.



13.5 Metareasoning budget
Exact value-of-computation calculation would itself be intractable.
ANANKE therefore caps metareasoning overhead at approximately 3–5% of total runtime.
It uses:
cached outcome statistics;
local influence cones;
learned ranking;
conservative action bounds;
periodic portfolio review.
If the scheduler becomes uncertain, it falls back to deterministic policies:
safety;
hard feasibility;
major decision-boundary uncertainty;
high-reuse abstractions;
fine optimization.



14. Human Architectural Sovereignty
ANANKE does not model beauty as a number.
It represents what the machine is permitted to treat as interchangeable.
14.1 Protected invariants
Examples:
sequence of compression and release at arrival;
views revealed at specific thresholds;
façade rhythm;
lobby proportions;
relationship between public and private zones;
deliberate asymmetry;
material continuity;
visible structural expression;
author-controlled irregularity.
A transformation violating a protected invariant is not penalized.
It is absent from the machine’s legal search language.



14.2 Approved equivalence classes
An architect may approve:
These 17 internal guestroom service layouts are experientially equivalent because none changes visible geometry, room proportion, sound character, or maintenance access from guest space.
ANANKE may then optimize freely among them.
The architect may refuse equivalence between two façades even if their energy and cost are identical.



14.3 Relational intent
Intent can be expressed through relations rather than target values:
space A must be perceived before space B;
view V must remain framed by surfaces S1,S2;
room width-to-depth relationships must lie in an approved family;
irregularity may occur only at specified narrative moments;
visible systems must remain subordinate to a material order;
circulation choices must preserve controlled ambiguity.



14.4 Negotiable territory
A negotiable transformation generates a human decision node:
Moving the core 0.9 m is estimated to save 2.1–3.0 million and reduce six structural transfers, but alters the protected lobby edge by 240 mm. Approve, reject, or redefine the invariant.
The machine does not quietly choose the exchange rate.



14.5 Human judgment as evidence
Architect approval is recorded as its own evidence type.
It is neither a mathematical proof nor a noisy score.
It states:
who approved;
what alternatives were reviewed;
what equivalence or exception was accepted;
under what project version;
what future changes invalidate that approval.



15. Adversarial Failure Intelligence
ANANKE attacks claims rather than running only random scenarios.
For claim h, it solves:
\[ \min_{\delta} \operatorname{PlausibilityCost}(\delta) \]
subject to:
\[ h(x,\delta)=\text{false}, \qquad \delta\in\mathcal P, \]
where \(\mathcal P\) is the admitted set of perturbations.
The answer is a minimum falsifying intervention.
15.1 Perturbation classes
correlated wind, rain, and power failure;
equipment failure plus blocked maintenance access;
construction tolerance plus supplier substitution;
abnormal occupancy plus controls failure;
flood plus disabled elevator;
fire plus open door and delayed detection;
maintenance neglect plus degraded filter;
utility interruption plus emergency-generator derating;
material substitution plus connection tolerance;
economic shock plus long-lead product unavailability.



15.2 Search methods
Depending on the claim:
mixed-integer adversarial optimization;
gradient-based local attack;
symbolic constraint solving;
reachability analysis;
scenario branch-and-bound;
rare-event importance sampling;
causal intervention search;
CEGAR over scenario abstractions.



15.3 Counterexample consequences
A counterexample may:
kill a witness;
kill an entire quotient class;
split a class previously considered equivalent;
invalidate a reduced operator;
add a new uncertainty variable;
create a new safety requirement;
expose a missing maintenance scenario;
force human reconsideration of a tradeoff.



15.4 Adversarial equivalence testing
Suppose two shaft systems were merged because their ordinary pressure-flow and space behavior matched.
The adversary asks:
Are they still equivalent when one valve is inaccessible?
Under a particular supplier substitution?
During partial construction?
With one riser isolated?
Under a firestop inspection failure?
During future conversion?
If a distinguishing context is found, the quotient class splits.
This is how ANANKE prevents compression from becoming wishful thinking.



16. Assurance Architecture
ANANKE uses a typed evidence lattice.
￼
16.1 Every elimination carries evidence
When ANANKE removes a design class, it stores:
the elimination rule;
assumptions;
relevant bounds;
competing class;
decision functionals covered;
tolerance;
proof or numerical certificate;
invalidation conditions.
The final answer therefore includes not merely:
Here are four good buildings.
It includes:
Here is why these four remain decision-relevant, why these other regions were eliminated, and where the argument is still incomplete.



16.2 Approximation influence
Every approximation states:
its validity region;
numerical error;
model discrepancy;
which claims depend on it;
which conclusions cannot be affected by its error;
what would trigger refinement.



16.3 Independent reconstruction
Final witnesses are regenerated through a separate backend:
independent geometric reconstruction;
fresh meshes;
fresh quantities;
alternate numerical formulations where practical;
model-disagreement tests;
independent code and clearance checks;
fresh uncertainty propagation.
The independent pipeline may run on the same workstation sequentially, but it must not reuse unverified optimizer conclusions as axioms.



16.4 No proof of physical reality
A machine proof establishes a property of a formal model.
It does not prove that:
the model is complete;
workmanship will match;
material data are correct;
a code official agrees;
a future hazard distribution is exact.
ANANKE preserves those distinctions permanently.

19.6 Engineering causal chain
The following consequences are synthetic:
Structural periodicity Two-room bays align with primary supports. Transfer or offset conditions fall from 7 to 1.
Façade rationalization Three façade modules fit one room pitch and six fit one structural bay. Unique panel families fall from 11 to 6.
Bathroom and plumbing alignment Wet-wall centerlines align with permitted structural penetration bands. Stack offsets fall from 18 to 3.
Drainage and domestic water Horizontal sanitary branches become shorter and more regular. Modeled horizontal drainage length falls approximately 16%, and hot-water recirculation length falls approximately 13%.
Corridor rack The same half-bay module becomes a rack shipping and support interval. Rack families fall from 7 to 3.
Duct-structure coordination A repeated service band avoids most deep-beam conflicts. Major duct/beam penetrations fall from 26 to 6.
Fan and equipment threshold Fewer fittings and shorter critical routes reduce modeled fan static by approximately 6.5%. A small envelope-load reduction from rationalized spandrel geometry combines with the pressure reduction to cross a real equipment-size threshold in the synthetic catalog.
Electrical consequences The smaller selected air-handling equipment reduces feeder and starter requirements, which slightly reduces electrical-room and pathway demand.

21. Why It Fits on One Workstation
It fits only if computation disappears in stages.
The following hierarchy is illustrative.
￼
21.1 Computation removed by symmetry
Identical rooms and floors are not independent design variables until an exception distinguishes them.
21.2 Computation removed by internal elimination
A detailed subsystem is replaced by the smallest boundary relation needed by the rest of the building.
21.3 Computation removed by contextual equivalence
Systems with identical admitted consequences become one class even if their internal geometries differ.
21.4 Computation removed by conservative bounds
A cheap lower bound can eliminate an entire abstract class.
21.5 Computation removed by operator reuse
A room or bay response is compiled once and reused across repetitions and nearby parameter values.
21.6 Computation removed by decision-influence stopping
A numerical uncertainty is not refined when it cannot cross a decision boundary.
21.7 Computation removed by persistent topology
A local rewrite reuses unaffected factors, operators, proofs, and solver state.
21.8 Computation removed by delayed commitment
Unresolved details consume almost no state until their differences matter.
21.9 Computation removed by a small output requirement
The machine is not asked to enumerate every good building.
It is asked to produce a tiny -choice-complete portfolio and evidence about what was excluded.
The honest limit
If the project has:
pervasive global coupling;
many unique spaces;
no repetition;
highly nonlocal architecture;
broad nonlinear hazards;
numerous incomparable human distinctions;
high decision-separator width;
then ANANKE will not fit comfortably.
It will merge less, widen separators, use more SSD, perform more conventional analyses, and possibly fail to achieve revolutionary compression.
There is no magic escape from intrinsic information.
The wager is that ordinary buildings possess far more causal sparsity, repetition, local behavior, and decision redundancy than current software exploits.

26. Final Verdict
Yes—this is conceptually stronger than Concordia, but only under a precise and falsifiable condition.
It is not stronger because it adds:
e-graphs;
abstract interpretation;
port operators;
metareasoning;
proof graphs;
adversaries;
abstraction learning.
Concordia could add all of those and remain Concordia.
ANANKE is fundamentally different because its authoritative object is no longer a design space, building family, or collection of candidates.
Its authoritative object is:
The coarsest evidence-bearing causal quotient that preserves every distinction capable of changing the final human decision.
That replacement causes several conventional distinctions to collapse:
design versus analysis: both become transformations of the same consequence circuit;
candidate versus family: both disappear into contextual equivalence classes;
geometry versus behavior: geometry becomes a witness for behavioral and architectural contracts;
optimization versus proof: optimization becomes progressive closure of decision regret with evidence;
simulation versus reasoning: simulation becomes one operation for refining a semantic relation;
solver versus model: solvers become generated backends of the compiled engineering theory;
search versus compilation: most “search” becomes variable elimination, quotient construction, and refinement.
The difference can be stated brutally:
Concordia tries to explore an enormous design universe intelligently.
ANANKE tries to prove that almost none of that universe deserves a separate computational existence.
If ANANKE’s runtime ultimately scales with the number of building families it visits, then it is merely a more complicated Concordia and should be rejected.
If runtime instead scales primarily with decision-separator width, while complete buildings appear only as late witnesses, then the conceptual leap is real.
That would mean researchers in 2026 were wasting most of their computation not because their solvers were slow, but because they insisted on distinguishing physical possibilities that were identical for every decision that mattered.
And that is the 30-to-50-year idea to bring back:
Do not compute the space of possible buildings. Compute the smallest theory that preserves the right to choose among them.
ANANKE-F: Formal Foundations, Semantics, and the Exact Finite Core
Abstract
This paper defines ANANKE-F, an exact finite core for decision-quotient engineering computation. ANANKE-F represents a partial building design as a typed finite program whose denotation is a finite set of well-formed physical realizations. It includes finite spatial and system topologies, finite geometric domains, products, construction and maintenance states, uncertainty scenarios, architectural sovereignty constraints, evidence records, and partially ordered human decisions.
The central relation is exact decision-relative contextual equivalence. Two compatible programs are equivalent precisely when replacing one by the other in any admissible engineering context leaves unchanged:
mandatory feasibility, safety, architectural-sovereignty, uncertainty, and evidence observations; and
every admitted human choice correspondence in every admitted menu of external alternatives.
The use of arbitrary external menus is essential: comparison of isolated objective vectors or singleton choices is insufficient when decisions exhibit thresholds, incomparability, menu dependence, or non-independence of irrelevant alternatives.
Five principal results are established:
THM-F1 — Context Congruence: equivalent subsystems remain equivalent in every admissible outer context.
THM-F2 — Quotient Composition Well-Definedness: composition descends to contextual-equivalence classes.
THM-F3 — Coarsest Decision-Preserving Partition: the contextual quotient is the coarsest partition through which every admitted observation and decision test factors.
THM-F4 — Finite Quotient Existence: under explicit boundedness conditions, every ANANKE-F contextual quotient is finite.
THM-F5 — Denotational Type Soundness: every well-typed program denotes only well-formed physical realizations of its declared interface type.
These results make the following statement mathematically precise:
Two partial physical designs may be represented by one computational state when no admitted physical, architectural, evidentiary, uncertainty, safety, or stakeholder-decision context can distinguish them.
The results concern exact finite mathematical models. They do not yet prove efficient quotient construction, physical model validity, compactness of realistic quotients, or the correctness of approximate or continuous compression.



1. Scope of ANANKE-F
1.1 Purpose
ANANKE-F is the deliberately finite semantic core of ANANKE.
Its purpose is not to approximate all building physics. Its purpose is to establish a universe in which the following objects can be defined without ambiguity:
partial designs;
concrete realizations;
typed interfaces;
physical composition;
engineering contexts;
structured observations;
partial human preferences;
architectural sovereignty;
typed evidence;
contextual equivalence;
quotient composition.
All sets used in ANANKE-F are finite. All numerical domains are finite. All recursive generation is bounded. All uncertainty is represented by a finite scenario set. Consequently, every semantic question in this paper is decidable by exhaustive computation, although the exhaustive procedure may be astronomically expensive.
1.2 Status vocabulary
The following labels are used strictly.
DEFINITION: introduces a mathematical object.
ASSUMPTION: restricts the finite universe being studied.
AXIOM: states a property required of an externally supplied primitive, model, checker, or admissibility policy.
LEMMA: proves a supporting result.
PROPOSITION: proves a result not designated as one of the five foundational theorems.
THEOREM: proves one of the central results under explicit assumptions.
CONJECTURE: states a desired result not established here.
ENGINEERING APPROXIMATION: describes a future nonexact implementation device.
EMPIRICAL HYPOTHESIS: states a claim that must be tested on physical or computational data.
1.3 What is finite
ANANKE-F supports:
a finite number of entities of each type;
finite spatial topologies;
finite structural and MEP topologies;
finite product catalogs;
finite domains for dimensions and capacities;
bounded repeated motifs;
finite construction-state graphs;
finite maintenance-state graphs;
finite scenario sets;
finite evidence graphs;
finite objective domains;
finite menus of alternatives;
finite sets of admitted decision functionals;
finite sets of admitted semantic contexts.
A finite grammar description alone is not sufficient. Unbounded recursion over a finite grammar can generate infinitely many realizations. ANANKE-F therefore imposes explicit bounds on entity counts and recursive unfolding.
1.4 What is not claimed
ANANKE-F does not establish that:
a formal building model accurately represents physical reality;
an engineering model has been validated;
realistic contextual quotients are small;
contextual equivalence can be computed efficiently;
continuous multiphysics systems admit finite exact quotients;
architectural beauty has been formalized;
human preferences are stable or rational;
physical evidence can be replaced by mathematical proof.
Its role is foundational: it defines exactly what later algorithms must preserve.

2.5 Boundedness assumptions
ASSUMP-F1 — Finite carrier bounds
For each sort (s), every realization contains at most (N_s) entities of sort (s).
ASSUMP-F2 — Finite attribute domains
Every geometry, capacity, cost, time, state, product, and scenario attribute has a finite domain.
ASSUMP-F3 — Bounded repetition

[ D_{\mathrm{rep}}\subset\mathbb N. ]

ANANKE-F admits no unbounded recursive generation.

ASSUMP-F5 — Canonical naming
Concrete realizations are stored as canonical representatives of interface-preserving isomorphism classes. Internal identifier renaming does not create a new realization.

The scenario set, model set, decision-functional set, interface-type set, and external-menu label set used by a fixed ANANKE-F theory are finite.

7.5 Associativity
PRO-F2 — Associativity up to canonical isomorphism
Suppose
[ p:\alpha\rightsquigarrow\beta, \quad q:\beta\rightsquigarrow\gamma, \quad r:\gamma\rightsquigarrow\delta ]
and all combined wirings are type compatible.
Then
[ (r\circ q)\circ p \cong r\circ(q\circ p). ]
Proof
Take realizations
[ x\in\llbracket p\rrbracket, \quad y\in\llbracket q\rrbracket, \quad z\in\llbracket r\rrbracket. ]
Both parenthesizations begin from the same tagged disjoint union
[ U_x\uplus U_y\uplus U_z. ]
The left parenthesization quotients first by the identifications between (y) and (z), and then by those between (x) and (y).
The right parenthesization performs the same two families of identifications in the opposite order.
In both cases the final equivalence relation is the reflexive, symmetric, transitive closure of the union of the two wiring relations. Closure of a union of relations is independent of the order in which its generating relations are added.
All transported relations and attributes are therefore interpreted on canonically isomorphic quotient carriers. Because compatibility is defined by the final combined structure, either both parenthesizations are invalid or both produce the same canonical isomorphism class.
Hence the two denotations are equal after canonicalization. ∎



7.6 Commutativity
Serial composition is not generally commutative.
For example, a pressure-reducing valve followed by a pump does not generally have the same boundary relation as the pump followed by the valve. Likewise, a construction event “install rack” followed by “close ceiling” is not equivalent to the reverse sequence.
Parallel composition satisfies a symmetry law:
[ p\otimes q \cong \mathsf{swap}(q\otimes p) ]
when the components have disjoint internal names and no imposed cross-component constraints.
Thus:
serial composition is generally noncommutative;
disjoint tensor composition is symmetric up to interface permutation;
undirected gluing can be symmetric when its wiring relation and physical constraints are themselves symmetric.

Thus replacing (p) by (q) changes the decision only in the presence of third alternatives.
This is why DEF-F46 quantifies over arbitrary admitted external menus and compares the entire chosen label set.



22.4 Geometry-only equivalence failure
Two service systems have identical geometry.
System (A) uses a valve replaceable from the corridor.
System (B) uses a valve whose replacement requires entering a guestroom and shutting down both rooms.
Their geometry is identical, but:
maintenance access differs;
outage consequences differ;
operational intent may differ.
Therefore geometric identity is neither necessary nor sufficient for contextual equivalence.



22.5 Nominal numerical-response equivalence failure
Two chillers have identical nominal:
capacity;
efficiency;
footprint;
cost.
Chiller (A) has independent failure modes across two modules.
Chiller (B) has a shared control board creating a common-cause failure.
Under the nominal scenario, their numerical responses are identical.
Under a control-failure scenario, their outage consequences differ.
Therefore equivalence must quantify over admitted uncertainty and failure scenarios.



22.6 Evidence-equivalence failure
Two analyses predict:
[ \mathsf{peakLoad}=500\text{ kW}. ]
For system (A), the result is enclosed by a conservative certified bound:
[ 490\le\mathsf{peakLoad}\le510. ]
For system (B), the result comes from an unvalidated surrogate with no applicability evidence.
The central predictions agree. Their evidence states do not.
A release decision may accept (A) and reject (B).
Therefore equal numerical predictions do not imply contextual equivalence.



22.7 Internal-count failure
Suppose a partial program contains ten internally different implementations, all producing the same observation profile.
If implementation diversity itself matters—for example because it provides supplier flexibility—then set-valued observations that deduplicate identical observations would lose relevant information.
The repair is not to retain arbitrary multiplicity automatically. The repair is to include a decision-relevant metric such as:
[ \mathsf{qualifiedSupplierCount} ]
in the observation structure.
ANANKE-F compresses only after the test theory declares what distinctions matter.



22.8 Budget-truncated context failure
Suppose contextual equivalence is defined using contexts of source size at most 100, while an outer context of size 80 is composed with a test context of size 60.
The resulting context has size 140 and may fall outside the bounded syntactic set. Congruence would then fail because the required composite context is not admitted.
The repair is DEF-F27:
admissible contexts are treated as a semantic category;
the context family is closed under composition;
semantically duplicate contexts are identified.
Alternatively, a resource-indexed equivalence would need an explicit additive budget theorem. That theory is deferred.
