24. Open Problems Exposed by Prompt 1
OP-F1 — Efficient contextual-equivalence checking
ANANKE-F equivalence is decidable by exhaustive testing. No efficient algorithm has been proved.
The number of contexts, menus, models, and scenarios may be exponential or worse in the source description.



OP-F2 — Finite distinguishing-context bounds
Given nonequivalent programs (p) and (q), determine a bound on the smallest context and external menu distinguishing them.
The current definition guarantees existence only because inequivalence is defined by an existing admitted test.



OP-F3 — Context-category generation
A semantic context category is finite but can be impossible to enumerate directly.
A constructive finite basis of contexts is needed.



OP-F4 — Observation adequacy
If an important safety, architectural, evidence, or decision variable is absent from the observation theory, the quotient may merge systems that future stakeholders wish to distinguish.
The correctness theorem is relative to (\mathcal T), not to all possible future meanings.



OP-F5 — Evidence dependency completeness
THM-FE1 is graph-theoretically exact. Its real semantic usefulness depends on AXIOM-F3: all true dependencies must be recorded.
Automatically discovering omitted dependencies remains open.



OP-F6 — Syntactic certification of intent preservation
THM-FS1 uses the semantic definition of an intent-preserving transformation.
A practical checker must prove that a finite rewrite certificate implies that universal semantic condition without enumerating every realization.



OP-F7 — Probabilistic and distributional decisions
ANANKE-F includes finite scenarios and rational weights, but contextual equivalence currently quantifies scenario by scenario.
Later work must distinguish:
robust equivalence;
distributional equivalence;
risk-measure equivalence;
decision-relative probabilistic equivalence.



OP-F8 — Resource-sensitive congruence
THM-F1 assumes context closure under composition.
A workstation implementation may admit a context only under a compute or memory budget. A resource-indexed contextual equivalence must track how outer-context composition consumes that budget.



OP-F9 — Continuous extension
Finite geometry and physics domains avoid measure theory, topology, numerical approximation, and limit semantics.
Extending the quotient to continuous and hybrid systems will require:
measurable observation maps;
topological or metric behavioral equivalence;
approximate congruence;
certified numerical envelopes;
continuity or robustness assumptions.



OP-F10 — Approximate contextual equivalence
ANANKE’s mature architecture requires merging systems whose differences are bounded but nonzero.
Prompt 1 proves only exact equivalence.
Approximate equivalence may fail transitivity unless the error structure is defined carefully.



OP-F11 — Compact quotient representation
THM-F4 proves finiteness, not compactness.
The quotient may contain nearly as many classes as source realizations.
The claim that real buildings admit dramatic compression remains an empirical and mathematical hypothesis.



OP-F12 — Witness extraction complexity
A quotient class may be decision sufficient while containing programs with difficult existential realization constraints.
Efficiently extracting a complete physical witness is not established.



OP-F13 — Dynamic test-theory refinement
When a new scenario, evidence obligation, model, or stakeholder decision is added, existing quotient classes may need to split.
An incremental refinement theorem is required.



OP-F14 — Physical model validity
ANANKE-F proves statements about model outputs. It does not establish that those models represent reality.
Formal proof, numerical verification, empirical validation, and physical measurement remain distinct.

27. What Has Now Been Proven
Within the exact finite ANANKE-F universe and under the stated assumptions:
A typed generative source language has a precise finite-set semantics. Every well-typed program denotes a finite set of canonical physical realizations.
Partial and complete designs are mathematically distinguished.
empty denotation means impossible;
singleton denotation means fully instantiated;
larger denotation means a realization family;
unresolved evidence or approval remains explicit.
Physical systems compose through typed gluing. Composition has:
typed compatibility;
identity systems;
associativity up to canonical isomorphism;
exact existential hiding.
Contexts are typed physical-program contexts. Plugging a well-typed subsystem into a compatible well-typed context produces a well-typed larger system.
Observations are structured. They retain separate:
hard feasibility;
engineering consequences;
architectural sovereignty;
safety;
evidence;
uncertainty applicability.
Human decisions need not be scalar, complete, transitive, or single valued. They are modeled as labeled-menu choice correspondences.
Architectural intent is not reduced to an objective score. Formal preservation concerns protected predicates, bounded variables, machine-free assignments, negotiable approvals, and architect-approved equivalence.
Evidence types are not collapsed into scalar confidence. Formal proof, numerical verification, empirical validation, physical measurement, code interpretation, and judgment remain separate.
Exact contextual equivalence is an equivalence relation.
THM-F1 proves substitution safety. If two programs are contextually equivalent, every admissible outer context preserves that equivalence.
THM-F2 proves quotient composition is well defined. ANANKE-F may compose equivalence classes rather than representatives.
THM-F3 proves the contextual quotient is minimal relative to the admitted test theory. Every decision-sufficient representation must distinguish at least the quotient classes.
THM-F4 proves the quotient is finite.
THM-F5 proves denotational type soundness.
The tiny hotel-bay model demonstrates a real quotient merge. Two internally distinct bracket products become one computational state because no admitted context, model, evidence test, scenario, or decision rule distinguishes them.
The tiny model also demonstrates a forbidden merge. Nominally identical equipment alternatives cannot be merged because a constrained maintenance context distinguishes them.
The principal sentence now has an exact interpretation:
[ p\equiv_{\mathcal T}q ]
means that every admitted mandatory test and every admitted labeled-menu decision test gives the same result after replacing (p) by (q) in any admitted physical context.
THM-F1 then proves that substituting one for the other cannot alter any admitted decision consequence in ANANKE-F.



28. What Has NOT Yet Been Proven
The following claims remain unproved.
Efficient quotient computation The exact finite procedure may require exhaustive enumeration.
Small quotient size Finiteness does not imply compression. In the worst case, nearly every realization may occupy a separate equivalence class.
Moderate decision-separator width No separator-width theorem has yet been defined or proved.
Approximate contextual equivalence Only exact equality is supported.
Continuous geometry or physics All domains are finite.
Certified reduced physics operators Port-envelope mathematics has not yet been introduced.
Knowledge transport across topology rewrites Rewrite-Functor Jets and generalized rewrite derivatives remain undefined.
Automatic abstraction discovery No theorem shows how a machine discovers sufficient separator variables.
Metareasoning optimality No value-of-computation theorem has been proved.
Witness-extraction efficiency A quotient class can be finite and decision sufficient while still being computationally difficult to realize geometrically.
Physical validity Mathematical equivalence under supplied models does not establish equivalence in the physical world.
Completeness of architectural intent THM-FS1 preserves only formalized intent.
Completeness of evidence dependencies The stronger interpretation of THM-FE1 requires AXIOM-F3.
Stability under test-theory expansion Adding new contexts, scenarios, products, models, hazards, or stakeholder decisions can split old quotient classes.
Global optimality Nothing in Prompt 1 establishes a globally best building.
The exact finite foundation is therefore complete enough to support later mathematics, but it does not yet establish ANANKE’s claimed computational advantage.
That advantage will require proving or empirically establishing that realistic engineering systems possess exploitable structure allowing the exact quotient—or a certified approximation of it—to be represented and refined without enumerating its concrete realizations.
ANANKE Mathematics Program — Prompt 2
The Engineering Myhill–Nerode Theorem, Canonical Decision Quotients, and Exact Finite Compilation
Abstract
This paper develops a finite many-sorted analogue of the Myhill–Nerode theory for ANANKE-F. The objects being minimized are not strings but typed, compositional engineering terms describing partial physical systems. Their observable behavior is determined by completion contexts, model and scenario families, mandatory feasibility and safety queries, architectural-sovereignty tests, typed evidence obligations, and stakeholder choice correspondences evaluated in arbitrary menus of competing alternatives.
The central construction assigns to each partial engineering term (p) its residual decision behavior
[ \mathsf{Res}{\mathcal T}(p) : \mathfrak E\tau \longrightarrow \mathsf{Outcome}, ]
the complete table of outcomes produced by every admitted engineering experiment compatible with (p)'s interface type (\tau).
Two terms are contextually equivalent precisely when their residuals are equal. This equivalence is proved to be a many-sorted congruence. Its quotient therefore inherits every source operation, including wiring, hiding, product choice, motif composition, process sequencing, intent restriction, and evidence attachment.
The principal result is the Finite Engineering Myhill–Nerode Theorem:
The contextual quotient is finite exactly when the admitted engineering experiment system has finitely many residual behaviors, exactly when a finite experiment-sufficient compositional algebra exists, and exactly when a finite reachable exact typed engineering recognizer exists.
The quotient algebra is then shown to be:
compositional;
reachable;
exact;
decision sufficient;
the target of a unique surjective homomorphism from every reachable sound representation;
minimal separately at every interface type;
unique up to a unique source-commuting isomorphism.
A finite-depth approximation sequence is constructed. It stabilizes after finitely many strict partition refinements. This yields:
a finite distinguishing context for every inequivalent pair;
a depth bound on such contexts;
an exact partition-refinement algorithm;
equivalence, distinguishability, and minimality certificates;
a canonical compiled artifact called the Finite Decision-Quotient Algebra, or FDQA.
The resulting theorem gives exact mathematical content to ANANKE’s core claim:
[ \boxed{ \text{ANANKE-F cannot be compressed below its contextual quotient without losing an admitted engineering distinction.} } ]
The theorem does not imply that the quotient is small or inexpensive to compute. It identifies the unique smallest exact compositional state space. Whether realistic engineering systems possess substantial quotient compression remains a structural and empirical question.

2. Scope and Assumptions
2.1 Two levels of the theorem
Two versions are proved.
General many-sorted theorem
The raw term algebra may be infinite. The contextual quotient is finite if and only if a finite exact compositional recognizer exists.
ANANKE-F corollary
The reachable denotational carrier is finite, so the quotient is automatically finite and can be computed by exact finite partition refinement.



2.2 Purity assumption
ASSUMP-MN1 — Pure compositional evaluation
Source terms are immutable mathematical expressions.
Implementation-level DAG sharing is computational memoization only. It does not imply that two occurrences denote one shared physical object.
Physical aliasing or shared identity must be represented explicitly through:
wiring;
shared entity identifiers;
containment;
aliasing constructors;
boundary identification.
This distinction is required for tree-term semantics.



2.3 Finite instantiated signature
ASSUMP-MN2 — Finite operation instantiation
For a fixed ANANKE-F compilation instance:
the interface-type set is finite;
the atomic subsystem library is finite;
the wiring library is finite;
guard predicates come from a finite admitted library;
intent theories and evidence attachments come from finite admitted sets;
repetition counts are bounded;
operation arity is bounded.
Derived macros are expanded into the finite primitive signature before quotient computation.



2.4 Complete terminal experiments
ASSUMP-MN3 — Experiment adequacy
Every distinction the theory promises to preserve is represented by at least one admitted terminal experiment query.
This includes every admitted distinction concerning:
feasibility;
safety;
intent;
evidence;
uncertainty;
stakeholder selection;
incomparability;

26. Canonicalization
26.1 Canonical up to isomorphism
THM-MN5 and THM-MN13 establish canonicality up to a unique source-commuting isomorphism.
This is the strongest representation-independent theorem.



26.2 Deterministic numbering relative to an input encoding
DEF-MN23 — Input-relative canonical numbering
Assume canonical orderings of:
sorts;
carrier states;
primitive actions;
terminal outcomes;
source representatives.
At every refinement round:
serialize signatures in that fixed order;
sort unique signatures lexicographically;
assign consecutive block IDs in sorted order.
The resulting quotient serialization is deterministic relative to the supplied canonical input encoding.



26.3 Absolute residual serialization
If:
the semantic experiment set is canonically enumerated;
every outcome has a canonical serialization;
then each quotient state has the canonical key
\mathsf{Serialize} \left( \mathsf{Res}_{\mathcal T}(p) \right). ]
Different quotient classes have different residuals, so the key is injective.
Sorting states by this key yields a byte-for-byte canonical artifact.
This construction can be prohibitively large because it serializes the full residual table.



26.4 Graph-isomorphism limitation
Without a canonical experiment enumeration or canonical source carrier, turning an arbitrary quotient transition hypergraph into a byte-identical serialization is a colored, many-sorted directed-hypergraph canonicalization problem.
That problem is not trivial and may contain graph-isomorphism-hard instances.
A practical implementation may therefore guarantee:
deterministic output for a fixed canonical input encoding;
mathematical canonicality up to isomorphism;
without claiming inexpensive absolute byte-level canonicalization.

28. Counterexamples to Weaker Definitions
28.1 Same direct observation does not imply equivalence
Compact and standard equipment have the same direct bay profile (z).
The depth-two replacement-clearance context distinguishes them.



28.2 Pairwise ranking is insufficient
PRO-MN0 constructs terms interchangeable under every two-item menu but distinguishable after introducing a third competitor.



28.3 Same numerical vector does not imply equivalence
Two designs may have equal:
[ (\mathsf{cost},\mathsf{energy},\mathsf{carbon},\mathsf{schedule}) ]
while differing in:
fire evidence;
maintenance access;
safety failure;
intent legality.
Mandatory reports preserve these distinctions.



28.4 Same current completed-building behavior does not imply partial equivalence
Two shaft subsystems may behave identically in one current five-story completion.
A ten-story completion with different isolation and pressure conditions may distinguish them.
Equivalence requires all admitted future completions, not one current project.



28.5 Arbitrary finite features are not automatically sound
Let
(\mathsf{cost}(p),\mathsf{energy}(p)). ]
Two terms may collide under (\phi) but differ under a maintenance or fire context.
Therefore a feature collision does not prove contextual equivalence.
Soundness requires:
[ \phi(p)=\phi(q) \implies p\equiv_{\mathcal T}q, ]
which must itself be certified.



28.6 Failure to find a counterexample is not equivalence
A heuristic search may test one million contexts without finding a distinguisher.
If the admitted context set contains an untested context, the two terms may still be inequivalent.
Exact equivalence requires:
a stable congruence certificate;
exhaustive finite refinement;
or another proof covering all admitted contexts.
Absence of a discovered counterexample is evidence of search failure or possible equivalence, not a proof.



28.7 Minimal scalar objectives are not minimal semantic states
Suppose two states have the same three scalar objective values but differ in how they respond to composition.
A downstream product threshold or safety context may distinguish them.
The minimal semantic state is determined by residual contextual behavior, not the number of scalar coordinates displayed to a stakeholder.



28.8 Quotienting before evidence obligations can be unsound later
Suppose two products are merged under theory (\mathcal T_1) because their physical predictions agree.
Expand the theory to (\mathcal T_2) by adding a mandatory validation-applicability query.
If one product has validated evidence and the other does not, PRO-MN5 gives:
[ \equiv_{\mathcal T_2} \subsetneq \equiv_{\mathcal T_1}. ]
The old class must split.
A previous quotient remains valid only for the theory under which it was compiled.

29.1 Exact finite decidability
PRO-MN6 — ANANKE-F contextual equivalence is decidable
For a fixed finite ANANKE-F instance, the algorithm ExactDecisionQuotient terminates and decides whether
[ p\equiv_{\mathcal T}q. ]

The finite carrier, operation tables, primitive action graph, and terminal output domains are finite.

29.2 What does not follow
This result does not imply decidability for:
unbounded recursive generators;

arbitrary nonlinear PDE systems;
unrestricted hybrid programs;
unrestricted natural-language requirements;
all future code interpretations;
all physically possible contexts;
arbitrary program equivalence.

bounded context classes;
conservative abstraction;
approximate congruence;
numerical error certificates;
counterexample-guided refinement;
explicit abstention when completeness cannot be proved.

Decision-Separator Width, Exact Factorization, and the Fundamental Complexity Theorem
Abstract
This paper develops an exact finite theory of decision-separator width for ANANKE-F. The objective is to determine when the complexity of whole-engineering synthesis can scale with the number of irreducible decision-relevant states crossing subsystem boundaries rather than with the number of concrete global realizations.
Prompt 2 established a many-sorted Engineering Myhill–Nerode theorem. For every interface type (\tau), it constructed the canonical quotient
T_{\Sigma,\tau}/\equiv_{\mathcal T,\tau}, ]
proved that this quotient is the unique smallest exact compositional state space preserving every admitted engineering experiment, and compiled it into a Finite Decision-Quotient Algebra.
The present paper restricts that theory to the exterior contexts of a region in a factorized engineering problem. For a regional semantic carrier (\mathcal X_L\subseteq X_\tau), the resulting canonical separator alphabet is
\mathcal X_L/\equiv_{\partial L}. ]
Its cardinality is the minimum exact number of messages that can pass from the region to its exterior while preserving Prompt 2’s complete repaired experiment semantics, including:
typed definedness and undefinedness;
joint model/scenario traces;
hard feasibility;
safety;
architectural sovereignty;
semantic evidence status;
uncertainty applicability;
arbitrary marked-candidate menus;
all admitted stakeholder choice reports.
The exact decision width of the separator is
\log_2|\Sigma_L|. ]
The main results are:
Separator sufficiency and minimality: (\Sigma_L) is the unique smallest exact separator semantics.
Communication characterization: (\lceil \log_2|\Sigma_L|\rceil) is exactly the deterministic one-way communication cost of the regional decision problem.
Exact dynamic programming: a fixed legal decomposition can be evaluated using only canonical separator states.
Fundamental complexity theorem: for decomposition node (v), with child separator-state counts (q_u) and local-choice count (\ell_v), exact running time is bounded by [ O!\left( \sum_v c_v\ell_v \prod_{u\in\operatorname{child}(v)} q_u \right). ] Writing (w_u=\log_2q_u) and (\lambda_v=\log_2\ell_v), this is [ O!\left( \sum_v c_v 2^{ \lambda_v+ \sum_{u\in\operatorname{child}(v)}w_u } \right). ] For branching factor at most (b), bounded local-choice width (\Lambda), and maximum separator width (W_D), [ T \le \operatorname{poly}(n,c) 2^{,bW_D+\Lambda}, \qquad M \le \operatorname{poly}(n) 2^{W_D}. ]
No-free-compression theorem: there are valid ANANKE-F families with (|\Sigma_L|=2^n), so exact semantic compression can completely fail.
Strict semantic advantage: there are nontrivial families with exponentially many raw states but constant decision width.
Discovery-gap theorem: small final decision width does not imply that the quotient can be found cheaply. Exact quotient discovery is coNP-hard even for compactly represented families whose final separator quotient contains at most two states.
Provisional-width law: exact bottom-up quotient compilation is governed in general by a provisional or discovery width (W_P), not solely by the final semantic width (W_D): [ T_{\mathrm{compile}} \le \operatorname{poly}(n) 2^{O(W_P)}, \qquad W_D\le W_P. ]
Thus ANANKE’s desired scaling law is correct in a precise nonuniform or precompiled setting, but it has a critical qualification:
[ \boxed{ \text{Small decision width makes exact message passing cheap; it does not by itself make the width discoverable.} } ]
The central unresolved real-world conjecture is therefore not merely that repetitive buildings have moderate decision width. It is that their moderate width can be discovered without traversing a much larger provisional state space.

Abstract
Prompts 1–3 established an exact finite semantic theory for ANANKE-F. Prompt 2 proved that every regional interface type has a unique smallest exact compositional semantics: its Engineering Myhill–Nerode quotient. Prompt 3 proved that, once exact regional separator quotients are available, whole-system decision synthesis over a supplied legal decomposition can be performed in time exponential in decision-separator width rather than in the number of global realizations. Prompt 3 also isolated the discovery gap:
[ \Delta_W=W_P-W_D, ]
where (W_D) is the width of the final canonical separator quotient and (W_P) is the provisional width incurred while discovering that quotient by explicit finite-state construction.
A quotient may contain only two states while exact quotient discovery remains coNP-hard from a compact source description. Small semantic width therefore does not imply efficient semantic discovery.
This paper develops an exact finite symbolic theory for attacking that problem. Its central objects are:
abstract engineering domains related to exact finite state sets by Galois connections;
sound abstract transformers for primitive engineering contexts;
symbolic predicates denoting potentially exponential state families;
exact symbolic preimages;
quotient-respecting partition refinement;
counterexample-guided abstraction refinement;
must-equivalent and may-equivalent relations;
proof-carrying abstract operations;
exact symbolic quotient certificates.
The main positive theorem is:
Structured Discovery-Gap Closure. If direct experiment fibers and canonical quotient classes admit compact symbolic representations; primitive-context preimages, Boolean set operations, satisfiability, and symbolic equivalence remain tractable; and refinement is quotient respecting, then the exact regional separator quotient can be discovered in time polynomial in the compact problem size and the number (2^{W_D}) of final semantic classes, without constructing the explicit provisional carrier of size (2^{W_P}).
More precisely, for (Q=|\Sigma_L|=2^{W_D}), (K) primitive context templates, maximum symbolic size (s^\star), and exact symbolic operation cost (C(s^\star)), a simple worklist algorithm requires
[ O!\left(KQ^2C(s^\star)\right) ]
time and symbolic space polynomial in (Q), (K), and (s^\star). The explicit concrete-state count (|X|) does not occur in this bound.
The corresponding negative theorem is:
Unless (\mathsf P=\mathsf{coNP}), there is no generic exact abstract compiler with running time (f(W_D)\operatorname{poly}(n)) for every compactly represented ANANKE-F region.
Thus symbolic abstraction closes the discovery gap only for grammars possessing a stronger property than small decision width. The required property is symbolic accessibility: compact class descriptions, closure under context preimages, tractable exact set operations, and bounded refinement growth.
The paper also proves that exact, fair, quotient-respecting refinement cannot lose a finite downstream butterfly effect. Whenever a local distinction changes any admitted complete engineering experiment, some finite distinguishing context exists, and symbolic refinement eventually introduces a predicate separating the affected states.
The exact chain established by Prompts 1–4 is therefore:
[ \boxed{ \text{compact source theory} ;\Longrightarrow; \text{symbolic state families} ;\Longrightarrow; \text{counterexample-forced distinctions} ;\Longrightarrow; \text{canonical separator quotient} ;\Longrightarrow; \text{decision-width dynamic programming}. } ]

52. Cover Construction Hardness
PRO-ER3 — Minimum Approximate Separator Cover Is NP-Hard in General
Even for a finite metric taking values in ({0,1,2}), computing a minimum radius-one representative cover is NP-hard.
Proof
Given graph:
[ G=(V,E), ]
define metric:
\begin{cases} 0,&u=v,\ 1,&{u,v}\in E,\ 2,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} ]
The triangle inequality holds because the only nontrivial case is:
[ d(u,v)=2, ]
and every two-edge path has length at least (2).
A radius-one representative centered at (u) covers exactly the closed neighborhood of (u).
A minimum radius-one cover is therefore a minimum dominating set of (G).
Minimum dominating set is NP-hard. ∎
ALG-ER4 returns a certified cover, not necessarily an optimal one.

62. What Has Now Been Proven
Under the explicit hypotheses in this paper:
ANANKE-F’s exact discrete semantic skeleton can coexist with continuous or numerical outcome spaces without weakening exact mandatory semantics.
Abstract family overapproximation, numerical error, parametric uncertainty, and model discrepancy are mathematically distinct objects.
Mandatory semantic disagreement has infinite distance and cannot be hidden by finite numerical tolerance.
The complete regional residual behavior carries a vector-valued contextual pseudometric.
Its zero-distance kernel is exactly Prompt 3 regional contextual equivalence.
Naive (\varepsilon)-closeness is generally nontransitive and cannot define an ordinary quotient.
The correct approximate separator object is a certified cover or residual codebook.
Its minimum representative-message count is the contextual covering number.
Approximate decision width is the logarithm of that covering number.
Approximate width is monotone nonincreasing in tolerance.
For finite exact semantics, zero tolerance recovers the exact separator quotient.
Primitive-context error propagates through certified transfer moduli.
Context-chain moduli compose, and scalar Lipschitz constants multiply.
A tiny local error may become globally large under amplifying contexts.
The exact Decision-Influence Error object is the set of mandatory or human reports that are nonconstant over the current enclosure.
A decision is stable whenever the whole enclosure lies inside one decision-report cell.
Error smaller than a positive decision margin guarantees exact report preservation.
Nested refinement eventually certifies every positive-margin decision.
Zero-margin decisions may remain unresolved forever.
Further numerical refinement cannot change a decision already certified over a containing enclosure.
Arbitrary choice correspondences do not define canonical numerical regret.
Bounded regret is valid only for decisions supplied with quantitative loss or utility structure.
An (\varepsilon)-choice-complete portfolio preserves qualitative reports exactly and quantitative decisions within declared regret.

67. What Has Now Been Proven
Exact interventional semantics
Engineering interventions can be modeled by finite many-sorted relations.
Typed action words compose associatively.
Interventional residuals preserve complete mandatory, evidence, uncertainty, and menu-sensitive outcomes.
Interventional trace equivalence is an equivalence relation.
Under action-context adequacy, interventional trace equivalence is exactly Prompt-2 contextual equivalence for the enlarged action theory.
Executable macro minimality
Exact one-step macro execution requires action-stable observation equivalence.
A finite canonical coarsest action-stable partition exists.
Its quotient is an exact reachable executable macro system.
Every other exact executable macro has at least as many reachable states.
Every minimum exact executable macro is isomorphic to the canonical quotient.
Executable bisimilarity implies equality of all interventional traces.
For deterministic total actions, trace and executable equivalence coincide.
For nondeterministic actions, trace equivalence can be strictly coarser than executable bisimulation.
Causal separator results
A Causal Sufficient Separator is an executable macro localized to a regional boundary.
Its width is the logarithm of the canonical executable state count.
Present decision width is no greater than causal width when future actions add distinctions.
If those actions were already part of the earlier context theory and the quotient is action stable, the widths coincide.
Adding interventions can only refine the causal partition.
Freezing hidden internals can reduce causal width.
Thawing them can require refinement.
Macro execution
Every finite admitted action sequence executes exactly in macrospace.
Every downstream experiment after that sequence can be answered exactly from the macro trajectory.
A closed macro need not reopen its fiber merely to determine successor macrostates.
Typed topology rewrites commute with an action-complete macro.
Macro synthesis results
Canonical quotient semantics and coordinate representation are distinct.
Bounded exact macro-program synthesis is decidable.
Minimum predicate-basis synthesis is NP-hard.
Unless (\mathsf P=\mathsf{coNP}), no generic exact macro compiler is FPT in causal width alone.
If interpretable synthesis fails, categorical quotient IDs remain correct.
Hierarchical and factored macro results
Executable macro layers compose hierarchically.
Locally minimal layers need not produce a globally minimal hierarchy.
A factored macro is exact only when its joint reachable relation is preserved.
Independent coordinate products can introduce impossible states.
Verified action footprints justify exact reuse of unchanged coordinates.
Sparse action footprints are not universal.
Symmetry and identity
Anonymous permutation-equivariant module actions admit exact histogram macros under the stated conditions.
Named actions can destroy histogram sufficiency.
Relative phase can be an exact executable macro when absolute translation is a symmetry.
Entity addressing is part of the action theory and can dramatically change causal width.
Rewrite integration
Rewrite execution at macro level is exact when the rewrite belongs to the certified action language.
Adding a rewrite may increase exact causal width.
Incremental action-theory refinement need split only unstable old macro blocks.
Full recomputation remains a sound fallback.
Approximate macro results
Approximate causal semantics must use action-stable covers rather than nontransitive approximate quotients.
A forward-simulating macro cover encloses every exact micro trajectory.
If its final enclosure is decision stable, the macro decision equals the exact micro decision.
Approximate causal width is a cover cardinality, not an equivalence-class count.
Complexity and hardness
Joint decomposition and causal-separator synthesis is NP-hard.
Macro online cost depends on causally distinguishable states, transition-program cost, thaw frequency, and fallback frequency.
Small causal state count does not imply easy expression synthesis or cheap transition evaluation.
Exact negative conclusions
Predictive sufficiency does not imply intervention sufficiency.
Passive observational agreement does not prove causal sufficiency.
One representative is not enough for arbitrary hidden-detail rewrites.
A full microstate can be the minimal executable macro.
In the parity-reset family:
[ W_D=1, \qquad W_C=n. ]
The deepest exact conclusion is:
[ \boxed{ \begin{minipage}{0.88\linewidth} The smallest state that preserves present engineering decisions need not preserve future design freedom. The smallest state that does both is the canonical observation-preserving, action-stable quotient induced by the admitted exterior experiments and intervention language. \end{minipage} } ]

[ M_{\mathrm{RAM}}(t) \le B_{\mathrm{RAM}}, ]
[ M_{\mathrm{VRAM}}(t) \le B_{\mathrm{VRAM}}. ]
Cumulative resource budgets and peak resource constraints are distinct.
A batch may reduce latency while increasing peak memory.
The semantic scheduler decides what information is valuable; the hardware scheduler decides when and where feasible computations execute.
They interact but are not identical problems.

45. Computation Upper-Value Bounds
A cheap upper bound

maximum effect of its macro coordinates.

[ \overline V(c\mid K)=0 ]
and no strategic side effect exists, (c) may be removed without computing a detailed RCVOC estimate.
If one computation has guaranteed net value greater than another computation’s upper value, the latter need not receive expensive meta-analysis first.



46. Value of Metareasoning
A metacomputation (m) refines estimates of:
[ v(c_1),\ldots,v(c_k). ]
Its value is the expected reduction in terminal loss caused by selecting a better base computation.
The same decision-stability principle applies:
if score intervals overlap in a way that can change the selected computation, meta-analysis may be valuable;
if THM-RC25 certifies one winner, further ranking refinement has zero current scheduling value.
This terminates recursive metareasoning at a certified computation-selection margin.

61. External-Menu Effects at the Meta Level
A computation is not irrelevant merely because it cannot change the current pairwise incumbent ordering.
It may:
discover a third alternative;
invalidate one alternative;
change incomparability;
alter the complete marked-menu choice set.
Qualitative closure therefore uses:
[ \mathcal R_q(K) ]
from DEF-RC13 rather than a scalar incumbent rank.



62. Mandatory Safety Is Not Scalarized
A computation resolving a mandatory safety obligation and one improving cost regret cannot be compared through an arbitrary dollar conversion unless governance explicitly authorizes such a policy.
The closure deficit and release gate retain mandatory blockers as hard conditions.
RCVOC does not permit life-safety obligations to be traded away for compute savings.

ALG-RC1 — CheckRegretClosure
INPUT

    theory fingerprint
    current authoritative portfolio
    closure policy

CHECK

    mandatory status singleton proofs

    evidence validity

    portfolio pessimistic utility bounds
    regret tolerance inequalities

    dependency hashes

RETURN

    NOT CLOSED with blocker set

ALG-RC2 — BuildLiveComputationAgenda
INPUT
    certified metaknowledge K
    dependency graph
    computation library
    resource limits

1. Compute G(K).

2. Identify all nonclosed obligations.

3. Compute the backward live cone.

4. Remove unavailable and theory-invalid computations.

5. Remove computations outside the live cone
   unless they alter future availability.

6. Replace recomputations by valid cheaper cache reuse.

7. Remove information-dominated computations.

8. Add prerequisite chains.

9. Mark mandatory-fairness computations.

10. Compute cheap value upper bounds.

11. Return the admissible live agenda.
Sound pruning relies on THM-RC4, THM-RC13, and THM-RC16.

INPUT
    live computation agenda

    scalar cost policy
    outcome metamodels
    fairness constraints

FOR each live computation c:

    compute Δc(1)
    compute:
        expected gain
        net value
        or gain/cost rate

MASK
    computations violating hard constraints

FORCE
    mandatory-fairness action where required

SELECT
    highest declared score

RETURN

LOOP
    run CheckRegretClosure

ALG-RC7 — DecisionDirectedFidelity
INPUT
    live quantitative or mandatory uncertainty
    current enclosure
    decision boundaries
    error decomposition
    available fidelity actions

1. Identify which decisions the enclosure can alter.

2. Identify the dominant error source:
       solver
       discretization
       reduction
       parameter
       model discrepancy
       evidence

3. Remove refinements unable to affect that source.

4. Estimate expected and guaranteed closure value
   of remaining refinements.

5. Choose the cheapest justified route.

6. Stop immediately when:
       mandatory state is exact
       and decision influence is empty.

7. Escalate to full solve or measurement only
   when cheaper certified stages remain inadequate.
Correctness of stopping is THM-RC21.

FOR each computation:

SELECT

AFTER UPDATE
    close every branch satisfying THM-RC17

INPUT
    candidate computation rankings

    metamodel refinement actions

IF one computation wins by THM-RC25:

OTHERWISE:

IF fingerprints and cost regime match:

ELSE IF compatible but shifted:

    (C : EngClaim)
    (A : Adversary C.ExactDb)
    (Gamma : Set C.ExactDb) where

def RobustOn
    (C : EngClaim)
    (A : Adversary C.ExactDb)
    (Gamma : Set C.ExactDb)

  ∀ ω ∈ Gamma,

      A.admissible ω α →
      ∀ ω',

        C.Holds ω'

75. What Has Now Been Proven
Claim semantics
Engineering claims are first-class exact report objects with explicit applicability, acceptance, evidence, and theory scope.
Universal, existential, equivalence, dominance, reuse, PCPE, macro, and release claims require different falsification objects.
One failed candidate cannot refute an existential claim.
Complete claim dependencies support exact invalidation.
Breaker correctness
A checked Claim Breaker soundly refutes universal adversarial survival inside the declared theory.
Proposal source is irrelevant to breaker correctness.
A surrogate, AI, or visual scenario is not authoritative without certification.
Robustness coverage
A checked universal coverage proof establishes that no breaker exists in the covered adversarial domain.
Failure to find a breaker on a proper tested subset is not a robustness proof.
Coverage labels distinguish safe, broken, unresolved, and outside-theory regions.
Search completeness and theory completeness are different.
Robustness radii
Scalar robustness radius is the infimum of certified breaker costs.
Finite nonempty breaker sets attain their minimum.
Compact closed breaker sets with lower-semicontinuous cost attain their minimum.
Open domains, nonclosed breaker sets, or discontinuous costs can produce unattained infima.
A breaker gives a certified radius upper bound.
Safe coverage below a radius gives a certified lower bound.
Closed-budget robustness is defined directly rather than inferred ambiguously from radius equality.
Pareto robustness
Vector-cost adversaries require Pareto-minimal breakers.
The Pareto breaker frontier can be exponentially large.
Scalar “smallest breaker” is undefined without a legitimate scalar cost.
Worst-case damage
Worst-case damage is monotone in adversarial budget.
Under positive-damage failure semantics, robustness radius is the first budget with positive worst-case damage.
Correlated hazards
Marginal hazard domains do not determine joint robustness.
Common-cause variables must remain explicit.
Failure ordering may be semantically relevant.
A failure multiset cannot replace a temporal failure sequence without a commutation theorem.
Causal attack cones
Perturbations outside a dependency-complete claim cone cannot change claim truth.
This enables exact pruning of adversarial search.
Macro-level attack reduction
Exact executable macrostates preserve breaker reachability.
Exact minimum breaker costs are preserved only when adversarial costs are also macro sufficient.
The claim-specific executable quotient is the unique smallest exact adversarial verification state space.
PCPE attacks
Universal properties established over a valid PCPE outer envelope hold for the exact subsystem.
Apparent breakers inside an outer envelope may be spurious.
Full-order validation is required for authoritative PCPE breaker claims.
Reduced-model certificates can be directly broken by one checked error-bound violation.
Evidence attacks
Evidence invalidation propagates through complete proof dependencies.
Evidence failure and physical failure remain distinct.
Minimum evidence-breaker selection is NP-hard for general AND/OR proof structures.
Construction and lifecycle attacks
Construction adversaries may require correlated geometry and event histories.
Lifecycle claims require explicitly time-indexed adversarial theories.
A commissioning certificate is not automatically a lifecycle certificate.
Adversarial CEGAR
Every breaker returned by the certified CEGAR loop is real.
Every robustness certificate returned by the loop covers the declared domain.
Spurious abstract breakers cannot invalidate real claims.
UNKNOWN remains unresolved.
Finite fair strict-refinement CEGAR terminates.
Symmetry and partial-order reduction
Group-orbit reduction preserves breaker existence and minimum cost when claim, transition, baseline, and cost are invariant.
Exact commuting failure actions need only one final-state ordering explored.
Named exceptions or transient claims can invalidate these reductions.
Local-to-global breaker lifting
A local breaker lifts globally only with a certified compatible completion and exact separator factorization.
Local failure without extendability may be globally impossible.
Compositional robustness
Independent conjunctive subsystem robustness composes by minimum only under strong product, null-attack, additive-cost, and no-interaction assumptions.
Cross-subsystem interaction can produce a composite breaker cheaper than either local failure radius.
Hardness
Breaker existence is NP-hard.
Exact bounded robustness verification is coNP-hard.
Minimum-cost breaker synthesis is NP-hard.
Minimum evidence-breaker synthesis is NP-hard.
Explicit finite nonnegative weighted breaker search is polynomial in the explicit graph.
Polynomial explicit-graph complexity does not imply compact symbolic tractability.
RCVOC integration
Prompt 10 exposes adversarial computations to the Prompt-9 scheduler.
Adversarial work outside the current live decision cone has zero current release value when it has no strategic side effects.
Both finding a breaker and proving bounded robustness may close live obligations.
Independent verification
Breaker and coverage artifacts have explicit independent checkers.
A release red team can search for exact databases contradicting closure certificates.
If such a breaker exists, the checker, certificate, dependency graph, or assumption theory is unsound.
The central doctrine is now formal:
[ \boxed{ \begin{aligned} &\text{breaker found} &&\Longrightarrow \text{claim invalid in the declared theory};\ &\text{coverage proof found} &&\Longrightarrow \text{claim robust in the declared region};\ &\text{heuristic search found nothing} &&\Longrightarrow \text{no theorem};\ &\text{UNKNOWN} &&\Longrightarrow \text{unresolved};\ &\text{hazard outside theory} &&\Longrightarrow \text{outside certificate scope}. \end{aligned} } ]

Claim-specific causal quotients remain small.
Symmetry reductions survive real named exceptions.

PCPE red teaming catches rare global modes without frequent cold fallback.
Adversarial CEGAR converges quickly.
Coverage artifacts remain small.
Robustness lower bounds approach known breaker upper bounds.
Minimum breaker costs correspond to meaningful resilience.
Perturbation cost functions can be governed consistently.
Probabilistic risk and adversarial robustness can be combined without confusion.
Prompt-9 RCVOC reliably schedules the most important red-team computations.
Whole-building adversarial verification fits the specified workstation.
Professional and regulatory stakeholders accept machine-generated coverage certificates.
The declared adversarial theory captures the hazards that dominate actual losses.
Search completeness can be achieved for realistic continuous domains.
Full-order physical validation remains affordable.
Adversarial portfolio reasoning remains tractable with many claims and objectives.
No theorem in this paper proves safety against every physically possible hazard.
